AUDIOJUNKIE: No new music this week!. No new music this week! So says my brain as I write this article. True enough there’s absolutely nothing new to be written about at this outing. I actually tried researching. I even bought a copy of Mojo magazine because of the cover, which depicted Depeche Mode at a youngish age. Then I realized there’s no new music coming from these UK synth heroes of mine in the past month or anytime soon. Well, there’s “Memento Mori: Mexico City” released in December of last year, so there’s that but no new music. How about Rush? The Canadian hard rock pioneers are back touring again where guitarist Alex Lifeson and bassist Geddy Lee got together with new drummer Anika Nilles. Rush’s Fifty Something Tour began in Los Angeles, California and is said to be knee deep in “thrills, deep cuts and tributes to fallen drummer Neil Peart.” Concert goers are enthralled so to speak with the shows at The Forum and is fast becoming the hot ticket tour of 2026. A customer of mine couldn’t stop talking about Nilles who took every Peart drum fill and wowed everyone who saw Rush at the concerts. Nilles , a German, paired well with Lee and Lifeson, who both seem happy up and about and playing live again. But seeing this as a greatest hits/tribute tour, no new music ever came out of it. But yeah, amazing tour! How about the news that beloved Dolly Parton passed away? The “Jolene” singer died last Tuesday at the age of 80 after a brief tussle with the big C, leaving her family and a seven-decade career as a global icon and humanitarian. Parton had many hits, among them “9 to 5”, “Islands in the Stream”, “I Will Always Love You” and even old ones like the Porter Wagoner duets like “Good As Gold”, “One By One,” and “Daddy Was An Old Time Preacher Man.” While many people knew her through her career as a musician and a movie star, Parton had a literacy program since the 90’s called the Imagination Library, where she donated millions of books to children. Parton had many memorable albums, but in 2023 she had released The Rockstar Playlist, wherein she had done duets with the likes of Ann Wilson (Heart), Rob Halford (Judas Priest), Sting, Steven Tyler, Peter Frampton, Paul McCartney and Ringo Starr. Parton was a multi-hyphenate in the truest sense of the word and all these artists would attest to that. Most of these artists will have a memory about Parton, but I guess Miley Cyrus really said something nice about her "fairy godmother" in a rather long quote. “The feeling of losing my Aunt Dolly is beyond what feels right to share. Our most sacred moments were private and they’ll stay there behind the stage, beneath the glamour and between our hearts. What I know is Dolly would want me to feel it, write a song about it, and then continue on and be strong. I have an angel by my side. I always have. One of our last conversations was about music and metamorphosis. I will always love her and want to make her proud. My heart breaks for the world, her family and friends who will miss her deeply. We’re in this loss together and we will see her in all of the most beautiful things.” Definitely no new music comes after that. But just in case, Emmylou Harris, Linda Ronstadt and Parton singing a cover of Neil Young's "After The Goldrush" would fill in the hole. Next week will be better.

Palawan Group celebrates its homegrown roots at Baragatan Festival 2026. * The Palawan Group of Companies proudly joined the celebration of the Baragatan sa Palawan Festival 2026, highlighting its deep connection to the province where its story began over 40 years ago. As one of Palawan's most anticipated annual events, Baragatan celebrates the province's culture, heritage, and unity, making it a meaningful occasion for the company to honor the community that has supported its growth from a single branch in Puerto Princesa into one of the country's leading financial service providers. Among the highlights of the company's participation in this year's Baragatan Festival were its participation in the Parada ng mga Palaweño and the Float Parade, where it joined communities from across the province to honor Palawan's history, culture, and traditions. Through its presence in these festivities, the company celebrated the spirit of togetherness that defines the province while supporting initiatives that preserve local heritage and encourage greater appreciation for the unique identity of the Palaweño people. Throughout the festival, the Palawan Group engaged with residents and visitors through its interactive booth, offering games, prizes, giveaways, and information about its products and services, including Palawan Pawnshop, Palawan Express Pera Padala, Palawan Gold, and PalawanPay. The activities provided an opportunity for the company to connect directly with customers while highlighting its commitment to delivering accessible, reliable, and affordable financial services. “Palawan is not only where our business began. It is where we learned the value of trust, resilience, and service to the community. The support of Palaweños has shaped who we are today, and we remain deeply grateful for the opportunity to grow alongside the province that we proudly call home,” said Karlo M. Castro, President and CEO of Palawan Group of Companies. Today, the Palawan Group continues to expand its reach across the country while remaining committed to promoting financial inclusion and creating economic opportunities for more Filipinos. Through its growing network and digital innovations, the company strives to provide practical financial solutions that help individuals, families, and communities achieve their goals. To make the celebrations even more festive, the Palawan Group gave special awards to the winners of Mutya ng Palawan 2026 in the form of PalawanPay Credits and ProtekTODO microinsurance, while the Grand Winner took home a 1-gram Palawan Gold coin. As it celebrates another Baragatan Festival with the people of Palawan, the company expresses its appreciation for the province it proudly calls home. While its presence now extends nationwide, the company remains rooted in the values and community spirit that shaped its beginnings, continuing its mission to serve Filipinos with trust, accessibility, and care.

Sweet sweep of fourth window makes Cone ‘the happiest guy’. Gilas Pilipinas head coach Tim Cone just couldn’t hide his elation after the Nationals pulled off what they initially believed an improbable task of sweeping the fourth window of the 2027 FIBA World Cup Asian Qualifiers against Iran and Jordan. Gilas hacked out a pulsating 82-81 escape against Jordan and then clamped down on world No. 26 Iran, 68-56, to improve the Nationals' record to 4-4, just a game behind their victims who are now on the third and fourth spots. “I’m almost lost for words. That’s really unusual for me. I’m not usually lost for words. But I’m extremely happy,” said Cone during the post-game press conference. “Kai just walked in (and asked), ‘Are you the happiest guy in the world?’ Because I said earlier, if we can win these two games, I’ll be the happiest guy in the world. So right now, I’m the happiest guy in the world,” he added. Playing without a naturalized player and with their World Cup fates hanging in the balance, Gilas showed steely nerves and unwavering resolve to complete the two-game home stand before a roaring crowd which braved through the rainy weekend to watch the team. The team also had to overcome two slow starts in the contests before digging deep and doing the game-winning plays when it mattered the most. “These are two really, really high-level international teams, Iran, especially. I read something in FIBA yesterday that this is only the third win we’ve had against them in the last 13 games,” said Cone “And we were able to do it all-Filipino pa. So it makes it really sweet to come out and win this game. And to do it at home,” he added. Gilas’ win over Iran is the team’s first win over the Middle East powerhouse in a FIBA-sanctioned tournament since 2015. Gilas also got several highlight performances from some of its players with CJ Perez and Kevin Quiambao spearheading the overtime win over Jordan, and Dwight Ramos and Juan Gomez de Liaño sparking the fourth-quarter pullaway against Iran. Kai Sotto was in his usual dominant form in the two games while AJ Edu remains the defensive lynchpin the Nationals can rely on. "It was one of those slow starts that we had but the guys just kept fighting and fighting and getting back into the game, and we came into halftime, we felt pretty good about ourselves. I think we felt we could pull this out,” said Cone. “Just a great character performance by these guys in both games. To have that overtime game. It’s easy to kind of let down coming into this one [against Iran]. But they all knew the importance of it. They all knew the importance it was for them, and for the country,” he added. "They came out and played and it was fun to be part of it. Really a lot of fun to be a part of it,” Cone furthered.

Pegula, Medvedev, Kostyuk make winning US Open start. NEW YORK (AP) — Jessica Pegula was one of the first players to compete at the U.S. Open, and she learned last year that starting Sunday, Aug. 30, provided some nice relief. “It is a little bit weird, but I did kind of enjoy that I could breathe for the next couple of days and everyone else is still freaking out about whether they’re going to win their first round,” she said. The head start is great — unless it's a head start back to the airport. “We were just talking about it, and I said, it’s so nice to play on Sunday when you win. But if you lose it’s not nice, because you feel like the tournament didn’t even start and you’re out of it,” No. 11 seed Marta Kostyuk said. Pegula and Kostyuk both won easily and now the get the benefit of any extra day of rest before returning for the second round. Novak Djokovic lost the first set as he began his quest for a record-extending 25th Grand Slam title on Sunday night against Mariano Navone. The match was paused during the first set so that the roof above Arthur Ashe Stadium could be closed because of rain that suspended play on the outer courts. Djokovic, 39, most recently lost his opening match earlier this month at Cincinnati. The No. 3-seeded Pegula beat Elena-Gabriela Ruse 6-3, 6-2. She said she was nervous early, which makes sense given what could be at stake for the 2024 U.S. Open runner-up. Pegula leads the women’s tour with 46 wins this season. She has two titles and has reached three other finals. Pegula can become No. 1 in the rankings if she wins her first major title and No. 2 Elena Rybakina loses before the semifinals. Pegula next faces the winner of the match between Venus Williams and fellow wild card Sofia Kenin. They were set to play in the nightcap at Ashe, and Williams and sister Serena are scheduled to play doubles together. “I felt really nervous before I went out there, but I know my coaches were like, ‘You didn’t really look that nervous. We thought you played great,’” Pegula said. The No. 11-seeded Kostyuk sure did, beating Storm Hunter 6-4, 6-1 for a strong start to the year's final major after reaching the semifinals at the French Open and Wimbledon. A Sunday start but the champions don’t begin until Monday It was the second year of a Sunday start, though some of the biggest headliners don’t begin until Monday. Two-time defending champion Aryna Sabalenka plays her opening match against Camila Osorio, before Carlos Alcaraz, who won his second U.S. Open title last year, plays his first singles match since April after recovering from a right wrist injury. Past U.S. Open champions Naomi Osaka, Iga Swiatek, Sloane Stephens and Stan Wawrinka are also on the Monday schedule, along with Wimbledon women’s champion Linda Noskova and men’s contenders such as Ben Shelton, Arthur Fils, Felix Auger-Aliassime and Frances Tiafoe. Daniil Medvedev, the 2021 U.S. Open champion, shook off his miserable preparation for the tournament by beating Hugo Gaston 6-4, 6-2, 6-4. The No. 7 seed was just 1-3 in the North American hard-court swing, usually a time he thrives. “Last couple of weeks was not easy,” Medvedev said. “But I’m happy that today I managed to produce high-level tennis.” Rain causes havoc, even in a stadium with a roof Other winners Sunday included No. 9 Elina Svitolina, No. 19 Jasmine Paolini and No. 31 Leylah Fernandez, the 2021 U.S. Open runner-up. No. 27 seed Barbora Krejcikova, a two-time Grand Slam singles champion, lost 7-6 (4), 6-2 to Kamilla Rakhimova. American Tommy Paul, the No. 20 seed, bounced back from losing a first-set tiebreak to Coleman Wong to win 6-7 (3), 6-1, 6-3, 6-3. Wong a year ago became the first man from Hong Kong to win an Open-era Grand Slam men’s singles match on the way to reaching the round of 32. Seven matches couldn't be completed because of rain — and one was delayed even though it was being played in the other stadium with a retractable roof. There was a mechanical issue with one of the sensors at Louis Armstrong Stadium, and even after the roof finally closed, the court had to be dried before No. 15 seed Alexander Bublik and J.J. Wolf could play. Maric Cilic, the 2014 U.S. Open champion, and 2022 runner-up Casper Ruud both withdrew with injuries. The U.S. Open is in the process of getting a new look Though the main draws didn't begin until Sunday, action at the U.S. Open has already been going on for nearly a week. Large crowds gathered for the mixed doubles tournament, an exhibition headlined by Roger Federer's return to Flushing Meadows and the singles qualifying tournaments, with admission to the grounds free. Fans who came for the first time Sunday may have noticed a tournament in transition. The U.S. Open is in the second year of a three-year renovation of Arthur Ashe Stadium, the main venue at the USTA Billie Jean King National Tennis Center. The improvements in the $800 million project include the addition of some lower-level seating, upgrades and additions of entertainment areas and the construction of a player performance center. “Please pardon our appearance while we are reimagining spectacular,” reads a sign above the entrance to Ashe. The project is scheduled to be completed in time for the 2027 U.S. Open.

Scheffler captures another FedEx Cup, surpasses Tiger Woods in career earnings. ATLANTA (AP) — Scottie Scheffler's second FedEx Cup title, and his 22nd victory on the PGA Tour during this astonishing five-year run, was different from all the others, even if it looked all too familiar. Scheffler celebrated with a beer. He had just closed with a 4-under 66 in the Tour Championship on Sunday, Aug. 30 — no one else from the leading six players broke par — and Scheffler had to wait for the last two groups to finish to make it official. “There was an open bar inside and I'm like, ‘All right, I’m grabbing a beer.' It tasted great,” Scheffler said. “I don't really drink often. My wife and manager were like, ‘Wow, I haven’t seen you have a beer in a long time.' Well, season's over now. I'm going to have a beer. Well-earned beer.” There was no arguing that, and there's no longer a debate over who had the best season in golf. Scheffler took care of that at East Lake when he made up a three-shot deficit in four holes and pulled away to win the Tour Championship, claim a second FedEx Cup title and move past Tiger Woods for most PGA Tour earnings. Scheffler signaled his rally with a 5-iron to within 2 inches of the cup on the 211-yard second hole. He caught Viktor Hovland with a 25-foot birdie on the fourth hole, pulled ahead for the first time on the 13th and wound up with a three-shot victory. It was his first time with the low 72-hole score at the Tour Championship. When he won in 2024, he had a two-shot lead before the tournament began given to the No. 1 seed under the “starting strokes” format. He won by four shots, even though two other players had a lower actual score. That still bugs him. “When you’re coming down the stretch of a tournament and you’re tied or one shot back, it’s different than when you’re adding it up at the end and there’s starting strokes and all that stuff,” Scheffler said. “I think having a real tournament to finish the year, where I am the winner and the lowest score at East Lake, feels like a bit more of an accomplishment.” Scheffler won for the third time this year — twice in the last three weeks during the PGA Tour's postseason — to match Chris Gotterup, Matt Fitzpatrick and U.S. Open champion Wyndham Clark for most titles in 2026. Players vote on the Jack Nicklaus Award for PGA Tour player of the year. Scheffler has won the last four years — another would tie him with Woods for most consecutive awards. Taking over the top spot in career earnings was inevitable. The $40 million purse at the Tour Championship now counts as official money. Scheffler won $10 million, pushing his career total to $130,390,661. Woods, who never played for more than a $10 million purse during his peak years from 1997 through 2009, had been at the top of the career money list for nearly 26 years. It was a small slice of redemption for Scheffler, who lost in a playoff to Hovland at the Travelers Championship, one of his five runner-up finishes this year. Hovland made only one birdie and closed with a 72 to finish alone in second, worth $5 million. Most aggravating for the Norwegian was having three putts hit the lip in a four-hole stretch on the back nine, two of them for birdie and one for par. “He’s just good, and he played good every day,” Hovland said. “I could have shot 66 easily as well today. Just didn't have it. ... It wasn’t like anybody else really played all that great in contention, and that’s what you see — a lot of guys just gagging and throwing up. And that’s where he just kind of stays in it and shoots a nice score. That gets the job done.” Scheffler had two bogeys — one an aggressive miss with a wedge from the fairway on No. 7, the other from a gnarly lie in the rough on the 14th — and otherwise felt he didn't miss much over a tough day of wind and firm turf that made the landing spots feel smaller. East Lake played to a cumulative average of 67.35 through three rounds. On Sunday, the average score was 70.07. Ryan Gerard, one shot behind Hovland staring out, made double bogey on the opening hole, followed with 13 straight pars and shot 72 to finish alone in third. “They made it as difficult as they could today, and that’s kind of what we were looking for,” Gerard said. “I just wasn’t on enough to execute shots to really tucked hole locations.” Scheffler said winning the Tour Championship for the FedEx Cup doesn't change his outlook on the season. That's for others to judge. Even so, he had a point to prove. He felt as though he had underachieved in the PGA Tour postseason — losing a six-shot lead to Rory McIlroy in 2022, not putting up much of a fight when Hovland won in 2023 when he started with a two-shot lead and finished 16 shots behind. “To come in this year maybe not winning the tournaments that I could have won throughout the regular season, to come in and win two out of three playoff events, is definitely a nice way to finish off the season,” Scheffler said. “That was my motto going into the playoffs. Maybe in years I’ve underperformed in the postseason, and maybe this is a year I’ll perform better than I have in the regular season.” That he did, and the beer no doubt went down smoothly.

Lacson says P3.713-B in public funds wasted on illegal Taguig reclamation projects. Senator Panfilo “Ping” Lacson said on Monday, August 31 that at least P3.713-billion in public funds may have been wasted on projects along areas of Laguna Lake in Taguig City that are subject to government action over “illegal” reclamation. Lacson said this latest finding will be among the pieces of evidence he and his team will send to the Office of the Ombudsman’s fact-finding team “for proper disposition" as his feud with Senate Minority Leader Alan Peter Cayetano continues. “WASTED PUBLIC FUNDS DUE TO MISUSE: Based on official records and our investigation, the total cost of Identified completed, ongoing (and suspended) DPWH Flood Control and Multi-Purpose Projects along the ‘illegal’ Laguna Lakeshore Reclamation Areas in Taguig City has so far reached ₱3.713 billion,” Lacson said in a post on X. https://twitter.com/iampinglacson/status/2094230183834484841 “These do not include other anomalous Slope Protection and Flood Mitigation projects along Taguig River involving double appropriations and 'ghost' projects using recycled photographs in different 'completed' projects, for billing purposes,” he added. Lacson, citing official records and his and his team's investigation, identified the top five contractors involved in projects covering P2.372-billion as: 1) Dahl Construction: ₱858.22-million covering five solo projects worth P571.5-million and four joint ventures totaling ₱286.7-million; 2) J.C. Uyecio: ₱483.1 million covering four joint ventures; 3) Toughbuilt: ₱434.2 million covering three solo projects; 4) Topnotch: ₱329.9 Million covering two joint ventures with Core Check and one with Beam Team; and 5) GR Fervidal: ₱266.6 Million covering five solo multi-purpose building projects Moreover, Lacson said all of the multipurpose building projects of GR Fervidal were suspended due to a “revision of plans” involving soil re-investigation. Earlier, Lacson said Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) Secretary Vince Dizon assured him that the DPWH would immediately issue cease-and-desist orders on projects linked to the illegal reclamation once he receives the appropriate requests from the Philippine Reclamation Authority (PRA). This is to prevent further waste of government funds on contractors carrying out unauthorized or illegal activities, he said. On Sunday, Dizon had said the DPWH has already issued the cease-and-desist orders, following a directive from the Office of the President coursed through the PRA. On Saturday, Lacson revealed that at least four parcels of illegally reclaimed land in Taguig City had been initially identified as covered by “fraudulently” issued land titles while at least four other parcels have no plotted title lots in the Land Registration Authority (LRA)'s digital file. Lacson was prompted to make the disclosure after Cayetano insinuated that his earlier findings on the illegal reclamation activities were “fake news.” But on Sunday, August 30, Cayetano, whose political bailiwick is Taguig City, said that the government stands to gain if allegations of illegally titled properties along Laguna Lake in Taguig are proven true. Speaking at the 44th anniversary of Mandaport Apostolic Pentecostals (MAP) Church, Cayetano said the roughly 18-hectare property could ultimately benefit the government if the allegation surrounding its title is established. “May isang nasa dyaryo kahapon na (nagsabi na may) 181,000 square meters o 18 hectares daw na ‘illegally titled.’ Sa isang banda po, nagho-hope din kami na totoo iyon. Bakit? Kasi kung totoong illegal iyon, sa gobyerno iyon (mapupunta), eh di may 18 hectares tayo ngayon para sa gobyerno (There was a report in the newspaper yesterday stating that there are 181,000 square meters—or 18 hectares—that are supposedly ‘illegally titled.’ On one hand, we actually hope that is true. Why? Because if it really is illegal, the property would revert to the government; that means we would have 18 hectares now for the government),” he said. The minority leader said he welcomes the scrutiny of land titles in the area, noting that City of Taguig Mayor Lani Cayetano had also long wanted the properties examined. “Katulad ngayon na gusto nilang tingnan lahat ng titulo, matagal na pong gusto ni Lani iyon ( Just like now, when they want to examine all the titles—Lani has wanted to do that for a long time),” he said.

Angelica Jones on Sachzna Laparan's cover of 'Miss Flawless': 'Nakaka-offend ‘yun on my part'. Former actress Angelica Jones opens up about her thoughts on the 2019 cover of "Miss Flawless" by Flow G and Bosx1ne featuring Sachzna Laparan. On the "Your Honor" podcast, the comedienne and politician said she and Sachzna originally planned to meet to discuss the use of the song. "Ang sabi nila magsu-shoot daw sa Laguna at makikipag-meet up. Meet up for shooting na, of course, ipapaalam muna (pag-revive sa kanta)... parang meron silang idi-discuss," Angelica shared. The meeting did not push through. "To be honest with you nakaka-offend ‘yun on my part kasi elected official ako and then nag-react ‘yung tourism ng Laguna na ang sabi ay hindi raw tuloy ang shooting, hindi raw tuloy ‘yung pagpunta nila doon,” Angelica said. She continued: ''Nalaman ko na lang na pumunta sila dun sa fourth district (sa Laguna), (doon) nag-shoot at ‘yung kantang ‘Miss Flawless’ (ginamit nila)." According to Angelica, she was asked by Lito Camo, who composed the song, if the group asked permission to cover the song. "Tinanong ako ni Kuya Lito Camo, tanong niya sa akin, ‘Bokal, nagpaalam ba sa sila ‘yo sila?’ Kasi sabi ko bago sila mag-shoot at ilabas ‘yung kantang ‘yan, magpaalam muna sa ‘yo,” she shared. Angelica had never met Sachzna prior, although she had seen her once at an awards ceremony. Still, Angelica said she would accept Sachzna’s apology if she offered one. "Wala naman problema sa akin puwede namang sabihin sorry, apologize. I will accept the apology kung meron pero as of now wala, e."

Dutch federation calls for FIFA summit, turns against Infantino. AMSTERDAM (AP) — The Dutch football federation is calling for an international summit to discuss the future of FIFA after becoming the latest nation to call for new leadership at the global soccer governing body on Sunday, Aug. 30. In a statement, the federation said it “no longer has confidence” in FIFA President Gianni Infantino, and offered to host an international summit to discuss ideas to reshape the organisation. The Dutch federation said there is a need for a “new FIFA,” not just a new president. “The 2027 presidential election should not only be about who leads FIFA,” it said. "First, we need to determine what kind of FIFA we want. Then we can identify the leadership needed to deliver that change. “For us, this discussion must be about more than Gianni Infantino. The key question is: what kind of FIFA does football need?” the federation said. “Our ambition is clear: a strong and credible FIFA that belongs to football, serves its members and develops the game around the world.” It said “this should not be a European plan for the rest of the world. We want to develop this new direction together with FIFA’s 211 Member Associations and the confederations from all parts of the world.” The federation said it shared “this position and our vision for the future of FIFA” in a letter to UEFA President Aleksander Ceferin. UEFA, the European soccer confederation, is spearheading the backlash against Infantino over his failed World Cup sell-off plan that created a deep rift in the sport. Many of its other member federations have withdrawn their support for the FIFA leader, who is up for re-election in March 2027. Some have called for his resignation. Infantino has not given any indication he plans to step down. “We believe FIFA needs new leadership from 2027 onwards. But a new president alone is not enough. The way FIFA is governed must change as well,” it said. “We see too much power concentrated around the FIFA president and insufficient separation between the president and the FIFA administration,” the federation said. “The process surrounding the now-withdrawn FIFA Forward Enterprise proposal was a turning point for us. Withdrawing the proposal was necessary, but it does not restore the trust that has been lost.” The Dutch federation said it sees three priorities: improved governance with a better balance of power, putting soccer’s social power at the heart of FIFA and investing more in soccer worldwide.

Armed man runs amok inside Baclaran Church. An intoxicated man carrying a loaded unlicensed firearm caused a commotion inside the National Shrine of Our Mother of Perpetual Help in Baclaran, Parañaque City, after he allegedly punched a security guard who tried to escort him out Sunday afternoon, Aug. 30. The 30-year-old suspect, identified by police as "Jenevie," a helper and resident of Imus, Cavite, was arrested at around 5:15 p.m. by personnel of the Baclaran Police Sub-Station. The incident occurred at the church compound along Redemptorist Road in Barangay Baclaran. Initial police investigation showed that a security guard approached Jenevie after noticing his suspicious behavior and apparent intoxication. When the guard attempted to escort him out of the church, the suspect allegedly punched him, triggering an altercation. Several churchgoers intervened and helped restrain the suspect until responding police officers arrived. Police said they recovered a .38-caliber “paltik” revolver loaded with one live round from Jenevie during the arrest. He was taken into police custody as authorities prepared charges for alleged violations of Article 155 of the Revised Penal Code (Alarm and Scandal), Article 151 (Disobedience to an Agent of a Person in Authority), and Republic Act 10591, or the Comprehensive Firearms and Ammunition Regulation Act. Meanwhile, the church clarified that no shooting occurred inside the shrine, contrary to reports circulating. National Shrine of Our Lady of Perpetual Help Rector Fr. Rico John Bilangel, C.Ss.R., said security personnel and police immediately responded to the commotion. Bilangel said two persons were injured in the incident and were promptly given first aid. He appealed to the public to refrain from spreading unverified information that could cause unnecessary fear and confusion among devotees and churchgoers. The rector assured the public that the safety and security of devotees remain the shrine’s top priority.

PIDS: Stronger institutions key to turning human capital investments into growth. The Philippines needs stronger institutions to turn increased investments and major reforms in education, health, social protection, and skills development into higher productivity and sustained economic growth, according to state-run policy think tank Philippine Institute for Development Studies (PIDS). In a recent discussion paper titled “Reshaping Economic Institutions for Transformational Partnerships in Human Capital Development,” PIDS said the country has strengthened its macroeconomic fundamentals and reached upper-middle-income status, but persistent gaps in learning, health-system integration, skills matching, enterprise participation, and productivity continue to hamper economic transformation. The paper was authored by PIDS senior research fellows John Paolo R. Rivera, Michael Ralph M. Abrigo, and Valerie Gilbert T. Ulep. “The Philippine development challenge is not the absence of reform,” PIDS quoted the paper’s authors as saying in an Aug. 30 statement. The constraint, they argued, lies in how investments are “coordinated, implemented, sustained, and evaluated,” PIDS added. The paper identified four interrelated institutional constraints: fragmentation and coordination failures; uneven implementation capacity; short policy horizons and weak credible commitment; and learning and incentive failures. These weaknesses limit the benefits of investments in human capital because education, health, employment, and productivity are closely interconnected. Educational outcomes, for instance, are influenced by health, nutrition, household conditions, and labor market opportunities, while skills generate greater economic value when businesses can put them to productive use. Innovation likewise requires not only capable workers but also enterprises willing to invest in technology and improve their operations. “Human capital is produced and utilized through an interconnected ecosystem and not through isolated sectoral interventions,” the authors said. As a result, investments in one sector may deliver lower returns when complementary investments in other areas fail to keep pace. The paper said fragmented investments can also prevent the government, businesses, households, and other stakeholders from realizing the full collective benefits of their individual efforts. PIDS thus called for a shift from a program-centered to an institution-centered approach to human capital development. Instead of focusing solely on higher spending or expanding individual programs, policymakers should strengthen institutions that allow investments across education, health, labor markets, innovation, and productive sectors to reinforce one another, according to the paper. “Government acts only as a financier or service provider but also as an institutional architect,” the authors wrote. In this role, the government establishes the rules, incentives, information systems, and coordination mechanisms needed to support collective action and encourage long-term investment. The paper also proposed what it called “transformational partnerships,” or institutional arrangements that enable multiple stakeholders to coordinate long-term investments in human capital and productivity. PIDS stressed, however, that the goal is not merely to establish more partnerships. Unlike conventional public-private partnerships (PPPs), which are often focused on infrastructure and service delivery, transformational partnerships emphasize sustained collaboration on complex development challenges that cannot be addressed by a single institution. “The policy objective is not more partnerships per se, but better institutions that enable productive partnerships,” the authors said. The paper identified five priorities to improve the effectiveness of human capital investments: better coordination around shared outcomes; credible long-term commitments; stronger institutional learning and information systems; better-aligned incentives for public and private investments; and greater capacity to implement and sustain complex reforms. “The Philippines needs continued investment in its people, but investment alone is not enough. Institutions must enable these investments to reinforce one another and produce lasting gains in human capital, productivity, and economic transformation,” PIDS said. “Institutional reform is itself a prerequisite for making human capital investment effective, sustained, and productive,” the authors said.

DOE: ₱11-billion geothermal fund draws 12 energy companies. The Department of Energy (DOE) is evaluating applications from 12 renewable energy developers seeking government financial assistance to expand geothermal power production. Energy Undersecretary Rowena Guevara said that 12 project developers have submitted proposals to tap a newly established ₱10.7 billion geothermal de-risking facility, While several initial applicants withdrew from the selection process, Guevara said the government has identified five alternative firms as backup candidates, signaling sustained private sector interest in capital-intensive deep-drilling operations. The financial mechanism is structured to absorb the initial capital risks inherent in early-stage geothermal exploration. Developers receive exploration funding in the form of a loan. If preliminary drilling fails to yield commercially viable steam fields, the debt converts into a non-repayable government grant, mitigating severe balance-sheet losses for private firms. Guevara said the DOE is sharing its shortlist of prospective applicants with multilateral partners, including the Asian Development Bank (ADB), as well as the Department of Finance and the Department of Economy, Planning and Development. However, Guevara declined to name the individual corporate applicants, citing ongoing evaluation procedures. But she revealed the prospective pool of developers includes foreign entities operating through joint venture structures with local companies, adhering to statutory ownership requirements. The ADB plans to launch an international tender to retain technical experts who will assist energy officials in auditing and evaluating the merit of each application. Approved in July, the ₱10.7 billion facility aims to unlock greenfield geothermal reserves across the archipelago. Unlike intermittent renewable energy sources such as solar and wind, geothermal installations supply continuous baseload electricity, making them vital for stabilizing the national power grid. Capital assistance under the program will allow approved developers to drill critical exploratory wells and accelerate preliminary site infrastructure. Alongside direct state funding, the DOE is backing legislative initiatives to grant enhanced tax and investment incentives to geothermal operators. The Philippines currently ranks as the world’s third-largest producer of geothermal energy, behind the United States and Indonesia, with an installed capacity of roughly 1,984 megawatts

DSWD spox to public: Check your facts on food pack cost before sharing. The Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) on Monday, Aug. 31, disputed the ₱1,503.84 price tag being circulated online for its family food packs, saying the figure referred to the maximum amount allowed for the procurement package, not the actual cost of each food pack. DSWD Disaster Response Management Group Assistant Secretary Irene Dumlao said the actual winning bid for the food packs cited in the post was ₱797.80 per box, submitted by 2 Go Global International Corporation. “₱797.80 lang ang halaga ng bawat kahon ng food packs na nasa post based on the winning bid. Kaya mali ang pinalalabas sa isang social media post na ₱1,503.84 ang halaga ng bawat family food pack ng DSWD (The food packs in the post cost only ₱797.80 per box based on the winning bid. Therefore, it is wrong to claim in a social media post that each DSWD family food pack costs ₱1,503.84),” Dumlao said. The DSWD spokesperson urged the public to direct questions or complaints to the agency and to exercise caution when sharing information from social media. “Hindi po nakatutulong ang mga ganitong misinformation, lalo’t higit sa panahon na ang atensiyon dapat ay nakatuon sa mabilisang pagtugon sa pangangailangan ng mga nasalanta (This kind of misinformation does not help, especially at a time when attention should be focused on responding quickly to the needs of disaster-affected families),” Dumlao said. “Nag-aappeal din po kami sa mga concerned citizens na siguraduhin ang inyong dokumento ay accurate sa inyong pagshare. Inuulit din po namin na ang DSWD ay bukas sa lahat ng komento at reklamo (We also appeal to concerned citizens to make sure that the documents they share are accurate. We reiterate that the DSWD is open to all comments and complaints),” she added. Dumlao said the amount indicated in the bidding document was based on market scoping and covered procurement specifications, packaging, logistics, delivery, and other factors related to the project. “We would like to clarify that the amount of procurement of family food packs differs per bid. The total amount spent for family food packs depends on the winning bid. The bid document which was posted is a public document and is the maximum bid amount of the package of items,” she said. She said the DSWD uses a simplified approach in procuring food packs to help ensure the availability and quick delivery of food assistance to families affected by disasters. “Dumadaan sa ‘competitive bidding’ ng DSWD ang lahat ng procurement ng family food packs kung saan ang may pinakamababang price bid offer at compliant sa mga specifications at iba pang requirements ang idinedeklarang bid winner (All DSWD procurement of family food packs goes through competitive bidding, where the bidder offering the lowest price while complying with the specifications and other requirements is declared the winner),” Dumlao said. Under the process, the DSWD Bids and Awards Committee evaluates suppliers based on their technical, financial, and legal requirements and determines the lowest calculated and responsive bid in accordance with government procurement rules. Each family food pack contains six kilograms of rice, four cans of tuna flakes, four cans of corned beef, two cans of sardines, five sachets of instant coffee, and five sachets of choco malt drink. DSWD said the composition of the food packs was endorsed to the National Nutrition Council and follows the Recommended Energy and Nutrient Intake formulated by the Food and Nutrition Research Institute. The contents are intended to provide affected families with a combination of staple food, protein sources, energy, and essential nutrients. However, the food packs are not intended to replace a family’s regular food supply for an extended period. DSWD said the food assistance is intended to help sustain a family of five for two to three days.

15,800 rescued across Luzon as ‘habagat’ rains trigger floods. More than 15,800 residents across Luzon were rescued and evacuated by the Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) as intensified rains from the southwest monsoon, or “habagat,” caused widespread flooding in several provinces. The PCG said its teams conducted simultaneous rescue operations and preemptive evacuations in coordination with local Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Offices. “Our ongoing efforts are supported by the anticipatory deployment of personnel, floating assets, land vehicles, and rescue equipment to strategic locations,” Commodore Noemie Cayabyab, the spokesperson of PCG, said in a statement on Monday, Aug. 31. According to the PCG, the advance deployment of its resources allowed response teams to reach communities affected by flooding more quickly. “These capabilities allow us to position response units closer to high-risk communities, shortening the time needed to reach families requiring assistance,” Cayabyab added. PCG Commandant Admiral Ronnie Gil Gavan credited the Coast Guard’s continuing modernization and additional equipment and personnel for its improved disaster preparedness. Also, he cited the provision of a Quick Response Fund, which enables the agency to address operational gaps and sustain its emergency response efforts.

PH, Brunei Darussalam sign MOU on strengthened judicial cooperation. The Philippines and Brunei Darussalam have formalized the agreement between the two countries to strengthen judicial cooperation in emerging, cross-border, and transnational legal issues. Areas of cooperation include the study of Shari’ah (religious and moral code of Islam), approaches to trafficking in persons, cybercrime and electronic evidence, and climate justice and environmental adjudication. Chief Justice Alexander G. Gesmundo and Brunei Darussalam Chief Justice Dato Seri Paduka Steven Chong led the ceremonial signing of a memorandum of understanding (MOU) at The Empire Brunei last August 30. With Gesmundo were Philippine Judicial Academy (PHILJA) Chancellor and retired Associate Justice Edgardo L. Delos Santos, PHILJA Vice Chancellor Sedfrey M. Candelaria, and PHILJA Academic Affairs Office Chief Emerito I. Enginco. A briefer issued by the Supreme Court’s (SC) Office of the Spokesperson stated that the MOU designates PHILJA and Brunei’s Judicial Education and Training Unit as the implementing institutions for the partnership. Under the agreement, the two judiciaries will cooperate in the exchange of expertise, knowledge, and best practices in judicial education, including curriculum design, teaching methods, and evaluation systems. They will also organize and participate in workshops, seminars, conferences, study visits, and other capacity-building programs for judges, judicial officers, and court personnel. The partnership also covers the development and sharing of educational resources, such as publications, research, bench books, training modules, and other learning materials; the undertaking of joint initiatives on issues of mutual interest, particularly emerging challenges affecting judicial administration and adjudication; and the facilitation of professional exchanges and networking opportunities to strengthen institutional ties and mutual understanding. In his message, Chief Justice Gesmundo said the MOU reflects the Philippine SC’s belief that the administration of justice is strengthened when judiciaries learn from one another. He also said the MOU is “an affirmation of the enduring friendship between our two nations and of our commitment to judicial excellence, rule of law, and effective delivery of justice.” He pointed out that the rapid pace of change requires judges and court personnel to engage in continuous learning and greater collaboration across jurisdictions. He also said: “Our courts today operate in an increasingly interconnected world. Legal disputes and criminal activities no longer remain neatly within territorial boundaries. Technological advances have transformed the way evidence is created, preserved, and presented. Environmental and climate concerns increasingly find their way into courtrooms. Artificial intelligence is reshaping institutions and raising profound questions about fairness, accountability, and the ethical exercise of judicial authority.” Gesmundo pointed out that the MOU’s greatest value lies in the stronger relationships it will foster between the two judiciaries. He stressed: “I believe the deeper value of this initiative lies in the relationships it will cultivate among our judges, judicial officers, judicial educators, and court personnel. Through candid dialogue and the sharing of experiences, we gain not only new knowledge but also a deeper appreciation of the circumstances and perspectives that shape another judiciary. In this regard, judicial education becomes a bridge, not merely between institutions, but between people and legal traditions, as well.” For his part, Chief Justice Chong described the MOU as a recognition that judicial education is strengthened through cooperation and the sharing of experiences among courts. Chong said: “The MOU reflects a shared recognition that judicial education is not simply an internal matter for individual judiciaries. It is an endeavor in which we can learn from one another, benefit from one another’s experience, and work together to strengthen the administration of justice.” He also acknowledged the Philippines’ contributions as co-chair of the Working Group on Judicial Education and Training under the Council of ASEAN Chief Justices (CACJ). “That role reflects the Philippines’ commitment to strengthening judicial education not only within its own judiciary, but also as an area of regional cooperation,” he also said. The signing of the MOU was a result of the discussions held during the recent Advanced Courses on the Role of International Law in Advancing ASEAN Judiciaries, hosted by the Philippines. The program brought together more than 100 delegates from ASEAN member states, including Brunei Darussalam. During the event held last February, representatives of the Philippine and Brunei judiciaries explored ways to deepen institutional cooperation and create more opportunities for judges, court personnel, and judicial educators to learn from one another.

Diesel drops by over ₱3.8 per liter starting Sept. 1. Motorists can breathe a sigh of relief at the pumps as oil prices drop during the first week of September. Effective Tuesday, Sept. 1, Shell Pilipinas will implement a ₱3.80-per-liter rollback on diesel and kerosene, alongside a ₱0.30-per-liter price drop for gasoline. Meanwhile, Seaoil will cut its prices by ₱3.83 per liter for diesel, ₱0.32 per liter for gasoline, and ₱3.84 per liter for kerosene. The Department of Energy (DOE) has yet to release the official price adjustments for oil companies this week, and average inventory data remains unavailable as of writing. A market expert earlier explained that the price cuts are driven by healthy supply following improved crude availability, though limited Middle Eastern exports have capped further declines. According to the source, gasoline prices remained below last week's levels but have been climbing due to tight regional supply. Even with an increase in Chinese exports, current supply remains inadequate to satisfy strong seasonal demand and ease prompt market tightness. As of last week, average prices stood at ₱76.90 per liter for gasoline (RON95), ₱89.40 per liter for diesel, and ₱118.10 per liter for kerosene.

Filipino youth urged to carry heroes’ legacy through peacebuilding. Office of the Presidential Adviser on Peace, Reconciliation and Unity (OPAPRU) Secretary Mel Senen S. Sarmiento on Monday, Aug. 31, called on Filipino youth to carry forward the legacy of the country’s heroes by helping build peaceful and prosperous communities. In his National Heroes’ Day message, Sarmiento said modern-day heroism is no longer limited to serving on the front lines but also involves creating conditions where lasting peace can thrive. “Today, the meaning of heroism has evolved. To be a hero in these modern times requires us not only to stand on the front lines. Instead, we are called to help create the conditions where genuine peace can firmly take root and flourish,” he said in a statement. Per Sarmiento, peacebuilding promotes economic opportunities, social justice, and community empowerment that can improve the lives of Filipino families. “Peacebuilding and heroism share a common goal. This is because fostering peace across our land paves the way for greater economic opportunity, social justice, and community empowerment, an environment that will create a brighter future for every Filipino family,” he said. The peace adviser underscored the role of young educators, entrepreneurs, and local leaders in transforming peace efforts into concrete development in communities. “When young educators teach in conflict-ridden areas, when youth entrepreneurs invest in marginalized communities, and when emerging local leaders bridge cultural divides, they turn the promise of peace into tangible progress,” Sarmiento said. “These young heroes must pick up the torch handed down by our forebears and show that peace and progress are mutually reinforcing pursuits, which are both essential to building stable, peaceful, and prosperous communities,” he went on.

Sarah Geronimo pregnancy buzz returns after Matteo Guidicelli's friend calls him ‘soon-to-be daddy’. Sarah Geronimo and Matteo Guidicelli are once again at the center of pregnancy speculation, this time after a friend of the actor appeared to let slip that Matteo could soon become a father. The buzz started with a Facebook post from a man who said he ran into Matteo at a coffee shop in Quezon City. Alongside a photo of himself with the actor, the man reminisced about their friendship, recalling their previous experiences together, including military-related activities. He described Matteo as a “solid guy” who is friendly and down-to-earth. Then came the line that sent fans into overdrive. “P.S. He is soon to be a daddy. Congratulations, bro!” the friend wrote. That was enough to get social media talking, with many immediately wondering if Sarah was pregnant with the couple’s first child. When someone directly asked if Sarah was expecting, the friend appeared to stand by his claim, replying: “Yup! Confirmed from the [horse’s] mouth.” The post was later deleted, but not before screenshots began circulating online. Still, neither Sarah nor Matteo has made an announcement confirming that they are expecting. The latest speculation comes after several other moments involving the couple had already prompted fans to play detective. One of them came when Matteo teased a vlog showing him undergoing an ultrasound, complete with a sonogram image. For a while, some fans wondered if the footage was a pregnancy clue. The mystery, however, was eventually cleared up when the full vlog showed that Matteo’s ultrasound was part of an executive check-up. Sarah was not with him during the procedure. Even Matteo’s birthday greeting for Sarah last July gave fans something to speculate about. “Happy birthday my love! This will be the best year ever,” he wrote. Some interpreted the message as a possible hint that something major was happening in their lives, while others simply saw it as a husband celebrating his wife. Sarah’s withdrawal from the first day of the Aurora Music Festival in May also resurfaced in online discussions. At the time, she was advised by her physician to take complete rest because of unforeseen health reasons. But there has been no information connecting that incident to pregnancy. What is known is that having children has been part of Sarah and Matteo’s plans for some time. In 2023, Matteo openly shared his hope that they would eventually welcome a baby. “For 2024 and in the future, sana magka-baby na kami. In God’s time,” he said. He also emphasized that while he was ready to become a father, he did not want to force the timing. Sarah expressed the same sentiment in an interview that year. “Siyempre ’yun po ang goal natin. In God’s time… In God’s perfect time,” she said. The couple married in a private ceremony in Taguig on February 20, 2020.

Romualdez says 'star witness' Guteza's first affidavit doubtful from the start. One-time Senate Blue Ribbon Committee witness Orly Guteza's first affidavit on the flood control mess was compromised to begin with. Former House Speaker, Leyte 1st district Rep. Martin Romualdez--whom Guteza accused of receiving cash luggage (maleta) payoffs from anomalous or "ghost" flood control projects--raised this point as he gave further context to the supposed "star witness'" eventual recantation. According to Romualdez, Guteza’s intial affidavit was already under a cloud before he took it back: The document’s supposed notary denied signing it, a Manila court treated it as falsified, and the people Guteza named as possible corroborators rejected the alleged cash deliveries. That's why the Office of the Ombudsman led by Jesus Crispin "Boying" Remulla cannot presume that Guteza’s first version is true, and then claim that his recantation is disputed, Romualdez's camp said. Romualdez's Supplemental Counter-Affidavit filed on August 20, 2026 said Guteza’s original account was never independently tested before a court. On page 17, he stated: “Even during the proceedings for the issuance of a Precautionary Hold Departure Order before the Sandiganbayan, complainant [Special Panel of Investigators (SPI)] did not present Guteza for personal examination, re-swearing, or independent verification.” "More fundamentally, the Guteza Recantation Salaysay does not introduce doubt into an otherwise stable and independently corroborated account," he said. In context, the supplemental filing argues that the earlier account was not stable or independently corroborated in the first place. Romualdez then listed the defects on page 18: “As already exhaustively demonstrated in my Counter-Affidavit, the Original Guteza Salaysay was already afflicted with substantial and independent defects before Guteza ever recanted it: the supposed notary expressly denied under oath having notarized or signed it; the document was subsequently treated by the Executive Judge of Branch 18 of the RTC of Manila as a falsified document; and M. Bunagan and Colesio—persons Guteza himself identified as capable of corroborating his narrative—executed sworn statements contradicting him and denying the supposed deliveries.” In 2025, the Manila RTC’s (regional trial court) executive judge cleared the named notary after a National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) examination found that the questioned signature and her standard signature were not written by the same person. The court referred the matter for further investigation. The supplemental filing also recounts Guteza’s new allegations about the preparation of his first account. “Guteza narrates that the supposed delivery narrative was raised during a meeting with former Congressman Mike Defensor, and that, despite his lack of personal knowledge of the matters being proposed, he was repeatedly pressed to adopt them. He further states that Defensor’s son-in-law thereafter reduced the proposed narrative into an affidavit on a laptop, and that sitting Senator Rodante Marcoleta subsequently reviewed and revised the document. "According to Guteza, it was in the course of that process that Sen. Marcoleta described his proposed account as the 'missing link' that would connect me to the alleged deliveries,” it said. The supplemental filing further underscored the importance of these attestations. “These details do not compel automatic acceptance of every accusation Guteza now makes. They do, however, render his subsequent account capable of examination and testing, and prevent his former account from rationally being treated as a stable and independent evidentiary foundation without confronting the circumstances he now describes.” No longer credible Meanwhile, lawyer Antonio “Audie” Bucoy, a former House impeachment spokesperson, reckoned that Guteza's original testimony, along with the allegations of the remaining 14 "Maleta Boys", were no longer credible. In an interview with DZMM radio over the weekend, Bucoy also claimed that the Ombudsman was resorting to “selective prosecution” and inexplicably targeting specifically the former Speaker. Commenting on the Ombudsman’s claim that it has 42 witnesses against Romualdez, Bucoy said the issue is not the number of witnesses but the quality and credibility of testimonies. “Hindi ho ito laban ng paramihan ng testigoy eh. Ito ho ay labanan ng kredibilidad at kalidad ng testigo. Ah gaya ho ng 18 (Maleta Boys), apat ang tumuligsa diyan. Pero pinanindigan nung apat kung bakit hindi totoo 'yung mga sinabi nila noon,” he said. (This is not a contest over who has more witnesses. This is a battle of credibility and the quality of the witnesses. For example, there were 18 [Maleta Boys], and four of them denounced it. But those four stood by their accounts and explained why what they had said before was not true.) He was referring to four Maleta Boys who have also withdrawn their original accusations against Romualdez. Bucoy said the retraction of the four jibed with the assertions of 25 Maleta Boys’ colleagues who were former aides of ex-Ako Bicol party-list Rep. Zaldy Co and who have belied the allegations of the original 18 Maleta Boys. But the most important retraction of all is Guteza's, Bucoy said. He pointed out that the 18 surfaced when Guteza suddenly disappeared days after his Senate testimony in September 2025. “Kung maalala niyo, ang una hong lumutang diyan ay si Orly Guteza. Nung bigla siyang naglaho ng hindi pa siya nasusuri ng mahusay, lumutang bigla yung 18,” Bucoy added. (If you recall, the first one to surface was Orly Guteza. When he suddenly disappeared before he could be properly examined, the 18 suddenly surfaced.) “Eh yan ho ay magkakaugnay eh. Kung pinabulaanan na ni Orly Guteza yung kanyang unang salaysay at sinabing ito ay pinilit lamang sa kanya at merong panunuhol na kaakibat ito, dagdag pa natin yung sinabi nung 25 na tinuligsa rin yung 18, ano pang kalalabasan nito? Wala hong ebidensiya. Hindi kapani-paniwala yung natitira,” he said. (These are all interconnected. If Orly Guteza has already denied his initial statement and said that he was merely forced to make it and that bribery was involved, and then we add what the 25 said, who also denounced the 18, what does this leave us with? There is no evidence. What remains is not credible.) Ombudsman choosing the evidence Bucoy also recalled that the original claims of the 18 Maleta Boys were directed not just against Romualdez but other lawmakers and public officials as well. He contends that the Ombudsman is choosing which evidence to use against which official. As such, he said he finds it surprising that the Ombudsman finds certain evidence credible against Romualdez, but lacking in weight against other officials. “Ang pinagtataka lang ho, ang aking personal na pagtataka, dahil ito ay sinusundan ko noon pa, ay bakit pinipili ng Ombudsman kung alin ang may kredibilidad, at alin ang wala. Pag ang tinutukoy na may pananagutan ay ang dating Speaker, sinasabi niya may kredibilidad,” the lawyer noted. (What I find puzzling, my personal concern, because I have been following this for quite some time, is why the Ombudsman chooses which accounts are credible and which are not. When the person being accused of responsibility is the former Speaker, he says the account is credible.)

Arana, Balti, RJ to bolster Gilas Asiad team. 10 yield ecstasy, other illegal drugs in Imus buy-bust. Color photos of occupied Japan face fading future. SENDAI, Miyagi Pref., Aug. 30 (Jiji Press) -- Color photographs of Japan under Allied occupation are vanishing more than 70 years after U.S. service members captured vivid scenes that may reveal forgotten fragments of history. From 1945 to 1952, when Allied forces governed Japan after World War II, U.S. service members stationed in the country photographed postwar Japan on color film, which was still rare in the country. Many of the photos are gradually being dispersed or lost over time, while some may contain historically significant scenes. An exhibition featuring color photos taken by U.S. service members was held in Sendai, Miyagi Prefecture, northeastern Japan, in August. The photos capture everyday scenes, including the area around a railway station, shopping streets and department stores decorated for the Tanabata festival, one of the three largest festivals in the Tohoku region of northeastern Japan, and Christmas. Their vivid colors are so striking that they look as though they were taken only recently with a digital camera. The photos are believed to have been taken by a U.S. Army officer stationed in Sendai with a camera made by Germany's Leica Camera AG and Eastman Kodak Co.'s Kodachrome reversal film. Fujio Chiba, 67, a senior official of a local history research association in Sendai, collected the photos on display. He searches for and acquires Japan-related photos and film through websites run by former U.S. military personnel and their relatives, photo-sharing sites and auctions. Chiba owns about 1,000 such photos, which show mainly cities where U.S. forces were stationed. Some vividly preserve places and objects that no longer exist. One photo whose photographer and date are unknown shows a monument marking the hypocenter of the Aug. 9, 1945, atomic bombing of the southwestern city of Nagasaki, capturing a white wooden pillar bearing the black inscription "marker of the atomic bomb hypocenter" atop a rounded mound. It precedes the current triangular black-granite pillar. Urakami Cathedral in the same city, which was heavily damaged by the atomic bombing, was rebuilt in 1959. A photo believed to have been taken in 1955 preserves a view of the cathedral's ruined state before reconstruction. Color film did not become widely available in Japan until after the 1964 Tokyo Olympic Games. Long before then, however, U.S. service members had been recording through color film the unfamiliar landscapes they saw through their viewfinders. Many of those service members have since died. Their children and grandchildren, who may have no particular attachment to the photos' subjects, sometimes leave the photos in cardboard boxes with other belongings or take them to antique shops as unwanted clutter. Some of those photos may preserve historical records that Japanese people themselves never documented, prompting Chiba to continue collecting them. "Photos tucked away among someone's belongings may have no value to their current owners but could be immensely valuable to Japanese people," he said. "I don't want them to end up as mere garbage."

BSP seen holding off on rate hike until 2027 as growth falters. Deutsche Bank AG expects the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP) to hold off on its next quarter-point interest rate increase until the first quarter of next year, as monetary authorities balance sticky inflation expectations against sputtering economic recovery. The Frankfurt-based bank’s forecast follows signals from monetary authorities that they are hesitant to tighten policy further immediately, choosing instead to prioritize economic growth following a series of domestic and external headwinds. On Aug. 27, the policy-setting Monetary Board (MB) decided to raise the benchmark borrowing rate by 25 basis points (bps) to five percent a move BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr. described as a decision that “wasn’t so hard” even as all other options were considered. According to the BSP, inflation could still flare up over coming periods given pressures expected from the looming El Niño and the potential implementation of a record-high ₱85 wage hike in Metro Manila. Such risks warranted “preemptive” policy action. While a boon to price stability, further raising key borrowing costs could add stress to the country’s productivity. Domestic economic growth slumped to a post-pandemic low of 2.3 percent in the second quarter, bringing the first-half average to 2.6 percent. Deutsche Bank believes further tightening remains on the table, citing the BSP’s elevated inflation assumptions for both 2026 and 2027. However, the German lender expects the BSP to defer further tightening from October this year to February 2027: “We think the BSP would prefer to watch for potential changes in inflation expectations or second-round effects from earlier shocks before making its next move.” Following its latest monetary policy meeting, the BSP now expects inflation to average 6.1 percent in 2026, down from its previous forecast of 6.4 percent. However, its inflation forecast for 2027 was raised to 5.4 percent from 4.5 percent. Both updated assumptions remain well above the BSP’s two percent to four percent target range. Headline inflation is expected to return near the three percent target by 2028. The revised outlook comes as inflation eased to 6.2 percent in July from 6.4 percent in June and a more-than-three-year high of 7.2 percent in April. For August, Deutsche Bank believes inflation may have fallen further to 5.8 percent “on the back of favorable base effects in food prices.” If realized, August inflation would reach a four-month low. Though forecasting higher figures than Deutsche Bank, Dutch financial giant ING and Singapore-based United Overseas Bank, Ltd. (UOB) also expect inflation to have softened to six percent on lower retail fuel prices. “Core inflation pressures, though, should remain elevated, with food inflation continuing to pick up,” said Deepali Bhargava, ING regional head of research for Asia-Pacific.

Old Australian courthouse finds new life as Nihon University facility. NEWCASTLE, Australia (Jiji Press) -- A 134-year-old former courthouse in Newcastle, Australia, is now a facility of Japan's Nihon University, with its preserved courtrooms offering students a hands-on lesson in the justice system. Completed in 1892, the former Newcastle Courthouse, distinguished by an arched entrance, is listed as a New South Wales cultural heritage site. After the court moved to a new building in 2016, Nihon University purchased the property and had it restored. The university has used the former courthouse since 2024, along with classrooms and lodging facilities built on either side. Courtrooms of different sizes, holding cells as well as rooms where defendants met their lawyers, remain in their original configurations. The defendant's dock in the former Grand Courtroom is enclosed by a wooden railing, with a dedicated staircase connecting it to the cell directly below. Students taking part in a study program in Australia in late August held a mock trial in the former Grand Courtroom. The smaller courtroom was named the Yamada Room after Akiyoshi Yamada, a former Japanese justice minister and founder of Nihon University's predecessor, Nihon Law School, which was founded in 1889. The university and the former courthouse date back to roughly the same period. "Preserving the site's historical value is meaningful," Takenari Shiba of Nihon University's office for internationalization promotion said. "We hope it will help students learn from the past." Haruhisa Ikenaga, a second-year student of the university's College of Law, said, "The courtroom felt authentic, and I gained a vivid sense of how it differed from Japan." Hana Harada, a second-year student of the university's College of Humanities and Sciences, said: "I saw cells for the first time. Scars on the walls prompted me to imagine the emotions of people who had been incarcerated there."

Level 5 heavy rain warnings briefly issued for 3 Fukui cities. TOKYO, Aug. 30 (Jiji Press) -- The Japan Meteorological Agency issued Level 5 emergency rain warnings for the cities of Fukui, Ono and Katsuyama in the central Japan prefecture of Fukui on Sunday, but later downgraded them. Level 5 is the highest on the agency's disaster alert scale. After the warnings were issued at 4:30 a.m., the three cities urged residents to take immediate action to protect their lives. The rain weakened later in the morning, and at 11:40 a.m. the agency downgraded the warnings to Level 4, before later lowering them further. The 24-hour rainfall reached 350.5 millimeters in Katsuyama through 9:10 a.m., 318 millimeters in the Miyama area of the city of Fukui through 11 a.m. and 281 millimeters in Ono through 11:20 a.m., all setting new record highs since observations began. Areas that received particularly heavy rainfall may face an increased risk of landslides due to loosened ground conditions. According to the Fukui prefectural government, many rivers overflowed, and flooding damage was confirmed at 16 homes in three cities and one town, including Ono and Katsuyama. A landslide occurred in the city of Fukui, while a sinkhole opened up on a road in the city of Sakai in the same prefecture. A woman in her 30s suffered a broken leg on a flooded road in the city. As of 10:30 a.m., prefectural police had received 106 reports involving stranded vehicles, flooding and other incidents. At a predawn press conference, Takuya Hosomi, director of the meteorological agency's Forecast Division, explained that a weather front extending from the Sea of Japan toward Fukui Prefecture had been fed by warm, moist air flowing northward around the edge of a high-pressure system over the Pacific Ocean, causing thunderclouds to develop. Hosomi noted that the situation was similar to the one that prompted Level 5 emergency rain warnings in five municipalities in Toyama and Ishikawa prefectures in central Japan on Thursday. However, he emphasized that, rather than extremely intense downpours occurring within a short period, very heavy rain of 50 to 60 millimeters per hour continued intermittently for a long time from Saturday night.

AUB approves ₱72-billion capital expansion to fuel digital payments push. Asia United Bank Corp. secured shareholder approval to nearly quintuple its authorized capital stock to ₱72.5 billion, laying the groundwork for broader push into digital payments and expanded lending operations During a Special Stockholders’ Meeting held Aug. 28, 2026, AUB reported that investors voted to amend the lender’s articles of incorporation, raising the capital threshold from ₱14.7 billion. The expansion, however, remains subject to regulatory clearance. Shareholders also cleared a 100 percent stock dividend. The distribution will satisfy the 25 percent subscription and paid-up capital requirement required to execute the capital stock increase, the bank said. Official record and payment dates will be fixed after regulators sign off on the plan. The capital injection is designed to give the mid-sized lender the financial leeway to scale up its commercial and consumer lending portfolios while deepening its footprint in financial technology. AUB has been building out its digital ecosystem, concentrating on its core e-wallet infrastructure and cross-border payment platforms. “The approval of our capital expansion marks a pivotal moment for AUB,” Abraham T. Co, AUB chairman, said. “Supported by our strong financial results, low cost of funds, and robust asset quality, we are laying the groundwork for sustained, long-term profitability.” Manuel A. Gomez, AUB chief executive officer, meanwhile, pointed to changing market conditions as the primary driver behind the aggressive digital push. “As financial landscapes rapidly evolve, we are doubling down on expanding our digital ecosystem by embedding cutting-edge technology into every facet of our operations,” Gomez said, adding that the goal is to secure new growth corridors and sustain technology-led profit momentum. The capital expansion follows strong earnings performance through the first half of 2026. AUB recorded a net income of ₱6.19 billion for the six-month period, underpinned by double-digit growth across its core banking activities. Total operating income climbed 10 percent year-on-year to ₱12.32 billion, fueled by a 14.9 percent gain in net interest income to ₱10.11 billion. Total loans and receivables expanded 10 percent to ₱281 billion over the same period. (James A. Loyola)

DigiPlus hires Teneo as strategic adviser amid global expansion plans. DigiPlus Interactive Corp., the country’s leading online gaming provider, has tapped global CEO advisory firm Teneo to help navigate domestic headwinds and drive its international expansion strategy. In a statement on its website, DigiPlus said bringing Teneo on board as strategic advisor reinforces its commitment to accelerating growth, strengthening its domestic foothold, and expanding its global presence. “The partnership comes at a pivotal stage in DigiPlus’ growth as the Company pursues opportunities beyond the Philippines,” DigiPlus said. The gaming operator noted that “Teneo will provide global perspective and senior counsel to help DigiPlus navigate complex business environments, assess emerging opportunities and risks, and make well-informed strategic decisions.” The collaboration underpins DigiPlus’ transition from a local market leader into a broader digital entertainment player. It also complements ongoing investments in innovation, responsible gaming, corporate governance, and operational capabilities—laying a stronger foundation for sustainable growth both locally and abroad. Leveraging its global team and network of senior advisors, Teneo delivers specialized services across five core business segments—offered independently or as an integrated service—to help clients address complex corporate challenges. Its global clientele includes a substantial roster of Fortune 100 and FTSE 100 companies, alongside major financial institutions and global enterprises. Abacus Securities Corporation noted that the advisory deal follows recent updates on DigiPlus’ ventures in Brazil and South Africa, as well as a license application in New Zealand. “The slow reception from its Brazil launch did not appear to stop PLUS from maintaining its strategy for its international expansion,” the brokerage said. However, Abacus pointed out that during a recent briefing, “management refrained from providing more clarity on the timing and strategies for its re-launch in Brazil and South Africa.” While noting it will take time to determine if hiring Teneo will yield tangible results, the brokerage emphasized that the move “shows the certainty of its plans to boost its international expansion.”

DepEd chief urges parents to help prevent school violence. Department of Education (DepEd) Secretary Juan Edgardo “Sonny” Angara has urged parents and guardians to take an active role in preventing school violence by closely monitoring their children and maintaining regular communication with school authorities, saying learner protection must begin at home and extend beyond the classroom. “Hindi natin kayang solusyunan ang karahasan sa mga paaralan kung sa loob lang ng classroom tayo kumikilos. Ang tahanan ang ating unang depensa (We cannot address violence in schools if we act only inside the classroom. The home is our first line of defense),” he said in a statement released on Monday, Aug. 31. The DepEd chief encouraged families to talk to their children daily, listen to their concerns, and coordinate with teachers and school officials. “Kausapin natin ang ating mga anak araw-araw, pakinggan natin ang kanilang mga pinagdaraanan, at makipag-ugnayan tayo sa kanilang mga guro at paaralan. Kailangan nating matutunang mapansin ang mga red flags at pagbabago sa kilos ng bata bago pa man umabot sa pananakit o bullying. Ipadama natin sa kanila na hindi sila nag-iisa (Let us talk to our children every day, listen to what they are going through, and coordinate with their teachers and schools. We must learn to recognize red flags and changes in a child’s behavior before these lead to violence or bullying. Let us make them feel that they are not alone),” he said. To strengthen parents’ participation in learner protection, DepEd said it is expanding its Kaagapay Program under DepEd Memorandum No. 002, series of 2026, and integrating it with the Parent Effectiveness Service (PES) Program under Republic Act No. 11908. The agency said the Kaagapay Program provides parent communities with practical tools through capacity-building sessions intended to help them identify warning signs, manage behavioral concerns, and coordinate directly with school Child Protection Committees and guidance personnel. Also, DepEd said it is working with the Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) to harmonize the PES modules with the Kaagapay Program. The partnership seeks to facilitate the full-scale implementation of the programs and address factors linked to violence, including mental health struggles and online safety risks. From July to November, the education department said it is also rolling out its program on Strengthening Collaboration of Parents and Teachers on Learner Protection in the Cordillera Administrative Region, National Capital Region, Cagayan Valley, Central Luzon, Calabarzon, Mimaropa, and Bicol Region. The initiative uses session guides developed by the DepEd Bureau of Learner Support Services-Learner Rights and Protection Division in partnership with ChildFund Philippines, Stairway Foundation Inc., and Meta Philippines. The training sessions cover online sexual abuse and exploitation of children, child sexual abuse and exploitation material, bullying and cyberbullying prevention, nihilistic violent extremism, parenting approaches, technology-based protective tools, and reporting and referral procedures. Trained regional and division Learner Rights and Protection personnel and education program specialists in values education are expected to lead the training of facilitators at the division and school levels. At the school level, DepEd said it is coordinating with Parent-Teacher Associations and School Governing Councils to incorporate parent education into existing learner protection measures and strengthen partnerships between homes and schools. “Shared accountability ang pagprotekta sa ating mga mag-aaral. Sa pagtutulungan ng paaralan, magulang, at komunidad, masisiguro natin na ligtas, nababantayan, at may nagmamahal sa bawat batang Pilipino (Protecting our learners is a shared responsibility. Through the cooperation of schools, parents, and communities, we can ensure that every Filipino child is safe, protected, and loved),” Angara said.

Kenyan runners stamp class in Pru Life UK run.
