Palace warns vs theft of pumping station equipment: Don't sabotage the President's projects. Malacañang expressed dismay over the reported theft of pumping station equipment which prevented operations amid severe flooding in Manila during the heavy rains. Without the stolen components, the pumping station could not operate, causing further floods, Palace Press Officer and Communications Undersecretary Claire Castro said. In a video statement on Monday, Aug. 31, Castro warned those behind the theft incident to stop sabotaging the President Marcos' projects. "Reminder, warning sa mga nagnanakaw. Nakakalungkot ito dahil ginagawa ng Pangulo at ng DPWH (Department of Public Works and Highways), MMDA (Metropolitan Manila Development Authority) at iba pang ahensya ang lahat ng paraan para maibsan ang problema sa baha (Reminder, warning to those who are stealing: This is saddening because the President, the DPWH, the MMDA, and other government agencies are doing everything they can to help alleviate the problem of flooding)," Castro said. "Huwag ninyong isabotahe ang mga proyekto ng Pangulo. Magtulungan po tayo Lahat tayo ay Filipino, maging mabuting Filipino po tayong lahat (Do not sabotage the President’s projects. Let us work together. We are all Filipinos, so let us all be good Filipinos)," Castro added. According to Castro, the President takes pride in the pumping stations that have been repaired and are now operational as these are among the reasons why floods subside more quickly in some areas of Metro Manila. The Palace official also expressed frustration over the incident, saying the government has to find the replacement of the stolen components once again and spend for replacements and repairs. "Pero dahil sa mga ninakaw ng mga halagang piyesa ng pumping stations hindi sila gagana. Gagastos tayo ulit para sa mga replacement na ito (But because valuable parts of the pumping stations have been stolen, they will not be able to operate. We will have to spend again to replace these stolen parts)," Castro said. "Paano kung walang makuha agad na replacement? Hindi agad maiaayos ang mga ito na magdudulot na naman ng mabagan na paghupa ng baha (What if replacements cannot be obtained immediately? These pumping stations cannot be repaired right away, which could once again result in flooding taking longer to subside)," Castro lamented. The Palace spokesperson stressed that the government’s efforts to prevent flooding are for everyone’s safety, urging people not to be selfish, as their actions could put lives, health, and property in communities at risk. "Ang ginagawa ng Pangulo para sa kontrabaha ay para sa ating lahat. Huwag tayo maging makasarili. Buhay, kalusugan at ari-arian ang maaapektuhan dahil sa mga pagnanakaw na ito (What the President is doing to address flooding is for all of us. Let us not be selfish. Lives, health, and property could be affected by these acts of theft)," Castro said. She warned those who are sabotaging the government that they will be held accountable under the law. "At sa lahat ng mga gumagawang pananabotahe na ito Kayo po ay hahabulin ng batas. Papanagutin po namin kayo dahil buhay at kabuhayan ang maaaring maapektuhan ng inyong mga makasariling gawain (And to all those carrying out these acts of sabotage: you will be held accountable under the law. We will hold you responsible because your selfish actions could put lives and livelihoods at risk)," Castro said. Public Works and Highways Secretary Vince Dizon said the Sunog Apog Pumping Station in Tondo Manila failed to operate during the heavy rains after electrical wires for the generator and its Meralco connection were allegedly stolen.

PH’s top surgeons to perform free simultaneous surgeries for over 200 patients nationwide. Close to 1,000 of the country’s top surgeons will render free surgery to more than 200 patients during simultaneous operations starting at 9 a.m. on Sept. 1, an advocacy the Philippine College of Surgeons (PCS) started four years ago aimed at addressing neglected or backlog surgeries for indigent patients across the Philippines. PCS President Joselito M. Mendoza, MD, FPCS, said the advocacy will include around 150 participating hospitals in the country and thousands of medical staff. Dr. Rouel Mateo M. Azores, PCS regent, said thyroid, Laparoscopic cholecystectomy (gallbladder removal), inguinal hernia repair, and other index cases will go under the knife at exactly 9 a.m. The National Surgical Outreach Day officially kicks-off the 90th anniversary of the PCS. “We reflect with pride on our rich legacy and look forward with renewed purpose and resolve. For nine decades, PCS has stood as the home of Filipino surgeons—committed to excellence, service, and the advancement of surgical care in our country,” Mendoza said. On Sept. 2, a Camaraderie Golf game will be held at the Camp Aguinaldo Golf Course at 6 a.m. On Sept. 4, a scuba diving and environmental awareness activity will start at 7 a.m. at the Solana Dive Resort in Anilao, Batangas. The PCS will install a stone marker on the seabed of Balayan Bay in the Municipality of Mabini, Batangas. “This is the PCS’s way of heeding the call for environmental conservation by way of coral regeneration and shoreline seabed cleanup to preserve our seas, bodies of water, and inclusive ecosystems,” Dr. Mendoza said. On Sept. 9, they will form a human monogram at the helipad of the new Ospital ng Maynila. On Sept. 11, the PCS will lead the National Stop the Bleed, a blood-letting activity, at its headquarters along EDSA in Quezon City. On Sept. 12, the PCS Foundation will hold a gala dinner at EDSA Shangrila Hotel and the awarding ceremony for the Lifetime Achievers, Legends of the Knife, Community Service, Young Trailblazers, and Most Outstanding Residents. The PCS is also set to unveil its 90th anniversary jubilee torch, its commemorative watch, and coffee table book “Kalayag” which is published by the Manila Bulletin.

MGen to ensure energy security in Panay Island. ILOILO CITY—Amid the ongoing energy woes in the Visayas, Meralco PowerGen Corp. (MGEN) has committed to ensure energy security of Panay Island. “We are ready to contribute to Panay’s and the Visayas’ energy security,” assured MGEN Thermal Energy Inc. President and Chief Executive Officer Arnel L. Santos. MGEN Thermal (formerly Global Business Power Corp). operates three coal-fired power plants in Iloilo City under its subsidiary Panay Energy Development Corp. (PEDC). While PEDC Unit 3 had an equipment failure last May 2026, it was able synchronize back to the Visayas grid its 150 megawatts (MWs) last July. The restoration was seen as a relief for the Visayas, which had been under red and yellow alerts. For months, there have been rotational power blackouts in Panay Island that particularly affected the city and province of Iloilo. “Recent yellow and red alerts across the Visayas have brought energy security and power supply adequacy back into sharp focus,” said Santos during an August 28 media forum in Iloilo City. During those times, Santos noted that PEDC Units 1 and 2 with combined capacity of 164 MWs as well as its two diesel-power plants in Aklan province with a 12-MW capacity were stable and operational. “Their sustained performance reflects our broader commitment to keep our facilities available, dependable, and ready to contribute to Panay’s and the Visayas’ energy security,” explained Santos. While having acknowledged the recent challenges faced by the Visayas grid, Santos said that MGEN Thermal Energy is working to do its share in preventing mass power disruptions. “This reminds us that reliable power should never be taken for granted. Every power plant, transmission line, reserve facility, and supporting infrastructure plays a critical role in keeping the system stable and resilient,” noted Santos. Joining Santos during the media forum were MGEN First Vice President and Panay Site Head Antonio Cabalhug Jr. and MGEN Retail Electricity Supplier Corp. Management Head Ralph Feliciano.

Man who told kin he'll end up at funeral parlor found floating in Ilocos river. LAOAG CITY, Ilocos Norte — The body of a man who had just been released from police custody was found floating on the Padsan River here on Sunday, August 30. Police identified the victim as Herminigildo Gaño, a resident of Barangay 9, Sarrat, Ilocos Norte. Gaño’s body was discovered floating in the river in Barangay 32-B, La Paz, prompting Barangay Captain Duldulao to alert the City Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office (CDRRMO). The CDRRMO immediately deployed its Search and Rescue Team, Medical Team, and other personnel led by Dr. Melvin D. Manuel. Rescuers, in coordination with the Philippine Coast Guard (PCG), recovered the body, which was reportedly clad a black striped shirt and black cargo shorts. Dr. Janine Ramos conducted an examination before the remains were turned over to the Philippine National Police (PNP) for investigation. Police said Gaño had been taken into custody in Sarrat on Aug. 28 because of his alleged violent behavior. He was released the following day, but reportedly refused to leave with family members who had gone to fetch him. Instead, Gaño allegedly ran toward the river and told his relatives that they would later find him at a funeral parlor in Laoag City. The statement took on a grim significance after his body was recovered from the Padsan River the next day. Police are investigating the circumstances surrounding Gaño’s death, including how he ended up in the river. It remained unclear if he drowned or if foul play was involved. The CDRRMO said it would continue responding to emergencies in the city, particularly as persistent rains have affected the area.

Charo Santos joins NSYNC dance trend, surprises fans. Charo Santos dancing to NSYNC? Well, why not? The veteran actress, best known for serious and dramatic roles, recently joined the latest social media dance trend to “I Want You Back,” and fans were quick to react. “Hindi tumatanda!” “Kaya makipagsabayan!” “Doesn’t look 70!” Of course, it is not every day that Santos, whose name has long been associated with weighty drama and intense performances, pops up on social media dancing to an *NSYNC song. But there she was. And fans clearly enjoyed seeing this side of her. The NSYNC Reel is not the only time Santos has been letting loose online. She is also having fun with her latest project, the short-form series “ Rich Boyfriend’s Mom ,” where she plays a wealthy mother determined to keep her son away from his girlfriend. It is a different kind of role for an actress so closely associated with drama, but Santos leans into it with the same commanding presence audiences know her for, only this time, there is a lot more mischief involved. And judging from the reactions online, viewers are having just as much fun watching her.

You don’t need to be famous to be a hero--Speaker Dy. Individuals of renown don't have a monopoly on heroism, as even common Filipinos can be heroes. House Speaker Isabela 6th district Rep. Faustino "Bojie" Dy III had this to say Monday, Aug. 31 on the occasion of National Heroes' Day. Amid rapid changes in society and around the world, Dy said Filipinos should hold fast to enduring Filipino values that have long defined the nation and its heroes. “Sa isang panahon na mabilis magbago ang mundo, kailangan nating bumalik sa mga pagpapahalagang hindi dapat magbago: katapatan sa salita at gawa, paggalang sa kapwa, malasakit sa nangangailangan, tapang na panindigan ang tama, at pagmamahal sa bayan,” he said. (At a time when the world is changing rapidly, we need to return to the values that should never change: honesty in words and deeds, respect for others, compassion for those in need, the courage to stand up for what is right, and love of country.) Dy added: "Ito ang tunay na mukha ng kabayanihan sa ating panahon.” (This is the true face of heroism in our time.) The Speaker emphasized that heroism wasn't reserved for famous figures or extraordinary acts; these be practiced by every Filipino through everyday acts of goodness and service. “Hindi kailangang maging tanyag upang maging bayani. Hindi kailangang gumawa ng pambihira upang makapaglingkod,” he said. (One does not have to be famous to be a hero. One does not have to do something extraordinary to serve.) “Kailangan lamang nating piliing maging mabuting Pilipino—araw-araw, sa bawat pagkakataon," Dy said in a poignant reminder to his countrymen. (We only need to choose to be good Filipinos—every day, at every opportunity.) According to Dy, National Heroes Day should serve as both a remembrance of the past and a reminder of the responsibility of the present generation. “Ang National Heroes Day ay hindi lamang araw ng paggunita. Ito ay araw ng pagpapaalala kung sino tayo bilang mga Pilipino,” Dy said. (National Heroes Day is not only a day of remembrance. It is a day to remind us of who we are as Filipinos.) “Ang ating mga bayani ay nag-iwan sa atin ng isang mahalagang pamana: ang paniniwalang may mga bagay na higit na mahalaga kaysa sa sarili—ang bayan, ang kapwa, at ang kinabukasan ng susunod na henerasyon.” (Our heroes left us an important legacy: the belief that there are things more important than oneself—the country, our fellow Filipinos, and the future of the next generation.) The Speaker said that responsibility now rests with today’s generation of Filipinos.

An unidentified man found dead in a hotel in Laguna. SAN PEDRO CITY, Laguna- An unidentified guest was found dead in his hotel room on Sunday afternoon, Aug. 30, in Barangay San Antonio, here. The body was discovered by a hotel staff when she tried to visit the room and, after knocking several times, there was no response. She reported it to her supervisor, who then checked the room but still received no response. At that juncture, they then forced the door open, whereupon they discovered the lifeless body of the male person inside the room. According to the investigation, the room was booked and was checked in on August 26, 2026, at around 2 p.m. by a certain Carlo, a resident of Brgy. San Vicente, San Pedro City, Laguna, for four nights until August 30. The victim is slim-built. Police secured the crime scene and investigated the victim’s identity.

33 dead, 19 injured, 3 missing amid cyclones, ‘habagat’—OCD. Thirty-three people died, 19 were injured, and three remained missing amid the effects of Tropical Cyclones “Luis,” “Maymay,” and “Neneng” and the southwest monsoon, or “habagat,” the Office of Civil Defense (OCD) reported on Monday, Aug. 31. OCD Disaster Preparedness Service Director Vicente Gregorio Tomas said during the briefing that the figures were recorded as of noon. “Ang mga namatay po, 33 po ang naka-record. Injured is 19. Missing naman po is tatlo (There were 33 recorded deaths, 19 injured persons, and three missing persons),” he said. Tomas added that 2.5 million families, comprising 8.8 million individuals, were affected by the weather disturbances. He identified Regions I, II, III, V, VI, IX, Calabarzon, the Cordillera Administrative Region, National Capital Region, and Mimaropa among the affected areas. According to OCD, a total of 1,365 evacuation centers were accommodating 46,900 families, or 164,500 individuals. “Number of evacuation centers totals to 1,365. Ang families po inside the different evacuation centers is 46,900, and individuals po is 164,500 (The number of evacuation centers totals 1,365. There are 46,900 families, or 164,500 individuals, inside the different evacuation centers),” Tomas said. As such, the OCD official reported that 3,300 houses were damaged, with 2,900 partially damaged and 405 totally damaged. “Sa damages naman po ay houses, 3,300; ang partially po doon ay 2,900; ang totally damaged naman po ay 405 (As for housing damage, 3,300 houses were affected; 2,900 were partially damaged, while 405 were totally damaged),” he said. OCD said damage to infrastructure reached ₱6.12 billion, while agricultural damage stood at ₱2.32 billion. According to Tomas, assistance provided to affected communities totaled ₱1.78 billion, while 117 areas were under a state of calamity. “As regards sa assistance provided po, in total po P1.78 billion, and of course the state of calamity is in 117 areas (Assistance provided totaled ₱1.78 billion, while 117 areas are under a state of calamity),” he said.

Whirlwind damages 10 houses in Ilocos Sur. VIGAN CITY, Ilocos Sur — At least 10 houses were partially damaged after a strong whirlwind swept through two villages in Burgos, Ilocos Sur, on Sunday evening, August 30. Ilocos Sur Provincial Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Officer Rhon Arquelada said the incident occurred at around 6 p.m. at the height of heavy rains brought by the enhanced southwest monsoon, or Habagat. No injuries were reported. The whirlwind struck Barangays Manaboc and Bangbangar, damaging the roofs of several houses and some garages and uprooting trees due to strong winds. According to the Burgos Municipal Police Station, barangay officials alerted authorities about the whirlwind while police were conducting situational monitoring in the municipality through handheld radios. Police personnel and members of the Municipal Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office immediately responded to verify the reports and assess the damage. Authorities assisted affected residents and helped move them to safer areas while clearing operations were conducted in the affected communities. Arquelada said the Provincial Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office remains on heightened alert as heavy rains associated with the Habagat continue to affect the province. As of 11 a.m. Sunday, at least 52 families from 15 towns in Ilocos Sur remained in evacuation centers for their safety amid the continuing heavy rains, he said.

Baguio records two deaths out of 585 dengue cases. BAGUIO CITY—The City Health Services Office reported two deaths from dengue, among the 585 dengue cases recorded from January 1 to August 15, lower than the 698 cases recorded during the same period last year. The two suspected dengue deaths involved a 31-year-old man and a 25-year-old man. With this, the CHSO urged residents to remain vigilant against dengue fever as the ongoing rains could create additional mosquito breeding grounds. City Health Officer Dr. Celia Flor Brillantes said dengue cases in the city remain below the city’s epidemic threshold despite an observed increase at the end of July. She warned that rainwater can accumulate in both natural and artificial containers, creating more potential breeding grounds for mosquitoes. Residents are encouraged to regularly inspect their homes and surroundings and remove stagnant water from containers, discarded items, garbage and other areas where rainwater can accumulate. According to the City Epidemiology and Surveillance Unit, dengue cases in the city have decreased by 16 percent this year. The analysis showed that the spread of dengue remains localized, with cases reported in 73 barangays during the four-week monitoring period. The CHSO continues to implement dengue prevention measures, including community clean-up drives, case investigations and information campaigns promoting the 5S strategy against dengue.

5 uncommon botanicals and functional foods. Are you taking multivitamins, omega-3 fish oil, herbal supplements, and the like? These products fall under a broad group of natural health products commonly known as dietary or food supplements. Marketing of food supplements, nutraceuticals, and other similar products has grown tremendously. This is primarily due to the increase in awareness of their advantages in preventive health. More people are also becoming inclined to adopt natural and alternative approaches due to the increasing cost of pharmaceuticals or medicines, as well as their negative side effects. According to Fortune Business Insights, the global nutraceuticals market size was valued at $547.68 billion in 2026 and is estimated to grow to $1,124.56 billion by the year 2034. That is more than double the increase in just eight years. Consumers, however, must be vigilant and not just fall prey to false marketing claims. Neither should a patient randomly take any nutraceutical product without the guidance of a registered nutritionist-dietitian and physician. According to the Implementing Rules and Regulations of the Nutrition and Dietetics Law of 2016, RA 10862, registered nutritionist-dietitians lawfully provide quality food and nutrition products, programs, and services aimed at optimizing the health and well-being of clients. Therefore, be wary of fake nutritionists and health coaches who recommend supplementation without the clinical background and professional license required by Philippine law. You may purchase nutraceutical products from laypeople, but always do so after consulting a Registered Nutritionist-Dietitian for proper guidance. It is important to understand the differences among various dietary supplements. These products may belong under one group for legal and commercial purposes, but they were created differently for various purposes and health benefits. Nutraceuticals are isolated bioactive compounds from food that provide medical and health benefits. An example would be the omega-3 found in fatty fish and resveratrol that is isolated and concentrated from plant foods that contain polyphenols, such as black grapes. Dietary supplements are concentrated, usually synthetic sources of nutrients such as vitamins, minerals, amino acids, enzymes, etc., that provide specific nutrients to correct deficiencies or bridge the nutrition gap when food intake is inadequate. An example is ferrous sulfate for iron deficiency anemia and ketoanalogues prescribed to kidney patients on a very low-protein diet. Botanicals are plants or parts of plants, such as leaves, flowers, bark, roots, seeds, or fruits, that have functional health benefits. Examples are turmeric root, ginger root, ginkgo biloba, and aloe vera. Functional foods are food or food ingredients that have additional health or physiological benefits beyond the normal nutritional values they provide (calories, carbohydrates, protein, and fat). Functional foods provide phytochemicals or plant nutrients, fiber, and antioxidants from plant food sources in wholesome form. When they are processed into liquid, freeze-dried, powdered, or pill form for convenience, they are known as modified functional foods. The Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics, formerly known as the American Dietetic Association, issued a position statement on functional foods: “All foods are functional at some physiological level, but it is the position of the American Dietetic Association (ADA) that functional foods that include whole foods and fortified, enriched, or enhanced foods have a potentially beneficial effect on health when consumed as part of a varied diet on a regular basis, at effective levels. The ADA supports research to further define the health benefits and risks of individual functional foods and their physiologically active components. Health claims on food products, including functional foods, should be based on the significant scientific agreement standard of evidence, and the ADA supports label claims based on such strong scientific substantiation. Food and nutrition professionals will continue to work with the food industry, allied health professionals, the government, the scientific community, and the media to ensure that the public has accurate information regarding functional foods and thus should continue to educate themselves on this emerging area of food and nutrition science.” Here are some uncommon botanicals and functional foods and their health benefits: Cordyceps sinensis and mycelium This mushroom contains polysaccharides (carbohydrates) that stimulate the immune system by increasing the production of natural killer cells to fight cancer cells and infections. It contains lectins that recognize and scavenge cancer cells. It also helps protect the kidneys and liver. Studies have shown that among post-kidney transplant patients, the phytonutrient cordycepin found in these mushrooms is associated with improvement in graft function, anemia, and leukopenia, and synergistically suppresses organ rejection by reducing drug-induced side effects. American ginseng This is different from Korean or Asian ginseng. American ginseng contains adaptogenic properties for stress, thereby enhancing sleep and promoting heart health. It helps with blood glucose regulation, immune regulation, and nerve regeneration. The phytonutrient ginsenosides also helps inhibit tumor formation. Hawthorn It is very rich in nitric oxide, which helps with heart health by regulating blood pressure, cholesterol, and triglycerides. It enhances blood circulation and sleep quality. Hawthorn has protective properties for the kidneys by reducing oxidative stress. Opuntia cactus Also known as prickly pear cactus, this plant has antioxidant activity that is seven times higher than the supplement vitamin C. It has 10,000 phytochemicals and antioxidants that increase the activity of the immune system’s natural killer cells. This plant reduces oxidative damage to the kidneys and liver, provides relief from digestive problems by coating the intestinal and stomach lining, and aids with blood glucose regulation and collagen formation. Therefore, it enhances skin integrity and lubricates the joints. Mangosteen pericarp The peel of the mangosteen has around 40 types of phytonutrients, xanthones. It acts as a natural anti-allergy by preventing the production of histamine in mast cells (immune cells). The peel cannot be eaten raw; that is why it is processed and taken in powdered or pill form. Berberine The bark and root of this shrub aid in regulating blood glucose, cholesterol, and triglycerides. It also has anti-inflammatory, antifungal, and antimicrobial properties. The phytochemicals in berberine trigger activated protein kinase, which improves the body’s metabolism. This plant promotes liver and gut health. When it comes to your health, don’t take chances. Let a health professional take care of you. Consult a health professional before purchasing and consuming any health product. cheshireque@gmail.com

Don’t be afraid to LARP. By Nicolette David 4th-year BFA Creative Writing student Ateneo de Manila University I recently traveled to Singapore with one of my girlfriends, and there was one Gen Z slang term we couldn’t stop saying: “LARPing.” We either called ourselves “LARPers” or our actions as larping, because everything we did on that short weekend vacation was exactly that. We posted Instagram stories a day or two late to make it appear as if we’d been there longer, dressed up to eat at a fancy restaurant that dented the bank, and paid almost ₱2,000 for access to the ever-so bougie Marina Bay Sands’ rooftop bar, Cé La Vi, to take photos of the city from way up above and pretend we’re hotel guests, even though we stayed somewhere three times cheaper. Basically, we were LARPing. What is larping? The term LARP or LARPing comes from “live-action role-play,” a type of role-playing game in which participants play fictional characters in real-life. Nowadays, LARPing, like its earlier meaning, refers to acting out a certain role in real life, essentially faking expertise or identity. It is now used in the same way that we call someone a “tryhard” or “performative.” In meme culture, LARP or LARPing is commonly used to mock people who flaunt a luxurious lifestyle that they do not actually own or can maintain. Gen Z is quick to judge people who create the illusion of financial success, particularly on social media, such as renting luxury items ranging from sports cars to designer bags or staying in expensive hotel lobbies or stores just to shoot dozens of photos and videos to post over a couple of weeks. Staging a high-luxury lifestyle is, without a doubt, a hardcore LARP. However, few people realize that there are smaller, perhaps unnoticeable, ways people LARP daily, especially if we go back to the term’s original meaning as performance. To LARP is to perform, but haven’t we been doing that already? Daily LARPs Take a look at popular aesthetics online, such as “clean girl,” “quiet luxury,” and so on. Many adopt an aesthetic archetype and put in the effort to showcase that lifestyle. People post online about their expensive workout classes or elegant clothing pieces, depending on what they want to be perceived as. We dress, eat, and live in a way that we want to embody. Another example of daily LARPing occurs in a workplace environment, where we can essentially fake expertise. I’m not talking about outright fraud, but rather faking confidence by sharing your opinions even if you’re shy or using workplace jargon to make people feel like you fit right in the job; but as we fake confidence, we can reduce the anxiety we may feel within. A form of LARPing that many already do is social media content staging. For instance, posting in upscale eateries or cafes, curating a photo dump to showcase only the cool, effortless-looking moments, releasing vacation photos days later to give the impression that you were there longer, posting in the gym like you’re an expert even if you’ve just started, or editing certain parts of a photo to highlight the best features of yourself. Like a vision board, you project a lifestyle that you might not have fully attained in real life. All of these small everyday self-conscious habits involve curating oneself to fit into a specific demographic. It may not be intentional, but it’s still a performance, and you could’ve just been LARPing this entire time. To LARP or not to LARP? But don’t start deleting all your social media posts or crying to your boss that you’re a fraud; there is nothing wrong with LARPing. As author James Pack said, “Life is a performance. Earn an ovation.” So, yes, the world’s a stage, but with that you can act with purpose because LARPing can go deeper than copying a chosen identity. Rather than simply focusing on how others perceive you, the motivation to embody a potential self can slowly but surely become more and more genuine. As the common saying goes, “fake it till you make it,” and if LARPing has the power to give you confidence to allow yourself to learn through performing as though you’ve already achieved your goals, then, as Gen Z may say: “Chat, I think I’ve found the method.” When you behave like the person you want to be and push through the unknown, you gradually let go of self-doubt and angst. Then, LARPing becomes a step toward becoming your best self. This is why I’m not ashamed to call myself a LARPer. I’ll walk into a steakhouse as if I belong there or into a luxury store only to try on items and add them to my future wishlist. At work, I’ll proudly state that I’m a confident person and use workplace jargon that I may or may not have just researched online. Funny enough, what started as a slang term, LARPing, motivates me to work harder, learn more, and face my fears because I can envision the life I want to achieve. Perhaps, when done right, LARPing is the way to bring out one’s courage to try and turn their dreams into reality? “Voices” is Manila Bulletin Lifestyle’s dedicated space for young writers and future journalists to speak up about the topics that matter to their generation—from pop culture and social trends to education, and everything in between. Have a story to tell? Join Voices! We’re accepting article submissions from young writers aged 25 and below, with each piece capped at 500 words. Send your work to lifestyle@mb.com.ph with the subject line “Voices: (Article Title),” or message us via Instagram at @manilabulletinlifestyle. Don’t forget to include a short bio with your age, school, course, hobbies, and any other details you’d like readers to know. We can’t wait to read your stories!

Historical, mordern heroes honored in Zambo celebration of National Heroes Day. ZAMBOANGA CITY- Zamboanga city joined the nation in commemorating National Heroes’ Day through a program held at Plaza Rizal on Monday, August 31. The program, which started with a flag raising ceremony, was participated in by officials and members of the security sector, government officials and personnel, Boy Scouts of the Philippines and academic institutions. During the program, officials honored both historic and modern day heroes as both offer their lives in service to the public. Mayor Khymer Olaso honored historical heroes and said that their heroism lives on through the modern heroes of today. "The true meaning of heroism is the willingness to serve others without expecting anything in return. We must do more for our city and continue to rise above every challenge, "Olaso said. Meanwhile, WestMinCom Deputy Commander BGen. Bayani Curaming, Deputy Commander for Internal Defense Operations said that heroism and courage from our national heroes continue to live on in the present time. Curaming lauded active-duty members in the security sector and civil servants who risk personal comfort to serve the public. "Let us show the nation that bravery born in August 1896 lives on in Zamboanga City," Curaming urged.

DSWD releases 2.3 million food packs to families hit by floods, landslides. The Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) has released about 2.3 million family food packs to families affected by successive storms and flooding, while maintaining millions more in reserve as the southwest monsoon or “habagat” continues to affect parts of the country. DSWD Secretary Rex Gatchalian said the 2.3 million food packs released over the past several weeks represent one of the largest relief distributions in the agency’s history. “That is one of the largest releases of family food packs in our history because we are talking about almost four weeks and 2.3 million food packs,” he added. Gatchalian said the DSWD would continue distributing and replenishing its relief supplies as more communities deal with the effects of recent weather disturbances. DSWD currently has 3,586,913 family food packs, 301,570 ready-to-eat food packs, and 282,931 non-food items prepositioned in strategic locations nationwide. The relief supplies are being used to augment assistance for communities affected by Tropical Cyclones Luis, Maymay, and Neneng, as well as recent flooding in Central Luzon and parts of the National Capital Region (NCR). DSWD field offices remain in coordination with local government units (LGUs) to monitor weather developments, assess emergency situations, and respond to requests for additional relief supplies. “The ones distributing to the beneficiaries or victims are the local government units because, remember, they are the first responders. We only provide augmentation,” Gatchalian said. “As far as we know, we have complied with all the requests we have received from local government units. But some local government units are already asking for a second or third round, and rightfully so, because this disaster has gone on for quite some time,” he added. Repacking hubs and supply chains nationwide continue to operate to replenish prepositioned relief supplies and ensure that resources remain available for communities affected by disasters.

P12.2M in presidential aid released to 61 Bacolod villages. BACOLOD CITY - This highly-urbanized city has released P12.2 million in financial assistance under President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.'s "Bawat Barangay Makikinabang” (BBM) program to 61 barangays for their socio-civic projects. Bacolod City Mayor Greg Gasataya, in coordination with the Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG) and the Office of the President, led the distribution of checks to representatives of all barangays during a recent ceremonial turnover at the Bacolod City Government Center (BCGC) lobby. Each barangay received a total allocation of P200,000, which included P100,000 for five Presidential Scholars, and P100,000 for a community development project identified by the barangay. Each scholar received P20,000 in educational assistance. Gasataya thanked the President and the national government for extending the program to all barangays, acknowledging the urgency and necessity of this program. He said this is the first time the national government has equally provided the Local Government Support Fund (LGSF) to all barangays, regardless of population and size. Gasataya also thanked barangay officials for their cooperation in completing the requirements necessary for the release of the funds, emphasizing that the program is intended to directly benefit their constituents. He required all barangay captains to submit signed certifications attesting that none of their selected scholars are family members or relatives of any incumbent barangay official. “This is to ensure that those who will benefit from the scholarship program are the ones who need it most,” the mayor stressed. DILG City Director Christian Nagaynay emphasized that accountability and transparency remain central to the program’s implementation. He noted that barangays are required to publicly post information on the distribution of assistance, including aid provided to scholars, and submit a fund utilization report every 30 days for the community projects they implement. The city government reaffirmed its commitment to working closely with barangay officials and national government agencies to ensure that the funds are utilized properly, efficiently, and transparently.

Body found in Muntinlupa identified. The body of a man who was pulled out from a drainage ditch in Muntinlupa last Aug. 27 was identified by his former live-in partner. The Muntinlupa police previously stated that the body of the man was discovered by a resident through an underground drainage opening under a bridge between Barangays Alabang and Bayanan. Personnel from the Muntinlupa City Fire Station’s Katarungan Fire Station needed to smash a hole on a sidewalk along the National Road in Barangay Bayanan to retrieve the body. Following the discovery, investigators made efforts to identify the body. Last Aug. 30, they interviewed J. Flores, 38, a scavenger. She claimed that she was a former live-in partner of the dead man who she identified as Efren Pineda Jr., 37, a scavenger. The police also identified Flores’ acquaintance, R. Valdez, 38, also a scavenger. She told the police that she gave clothes to Pineda consisting of a yellow green polo shirt and dark blue pants. Together with the police, Flores and Valdez went to Our Lady of Loreto Funeral Homes in Taguig City to identify the body. According to the police, the two women positively identified the body even though it was in an advanced stage of decomposition based on his clothes, which were the ones Valdez gave to him. Flores also identified the body through a bump in the right upper forehead. Flores said Pineda engaged in scavenging activities in Bayanan, telling the police that he would frequently go underneath the creek and in the drainage canal. She said she had an argument with Pineda last Aug. 2, the last time she saw Pineda alive. After this, she said, he went to the underground drainage canal where his body was later discovered. The Muntinlupa police are exerting efforts to locate Pineda’s family and relatives

Arm cache unearthed in Quezon. LOPEZ, Quezon- An arm cache belonging to the New People’s Army (NPA) was unearthed by government forces in Barangay Santa Rosa on Friday, Aug. 28, in this town. According to the report of the 201st Infantry Brigade, the combined forces of the 85th Infantry Battalion, the 417th Quezon Police Mobile Force Company, and the Lopez Municipal Police Station discovered the arms cache following information given by a former rebel. The location of the arms cache was revealed by a rebel returnee who disclosed that following an armed encounter between the government forces and the NPA rebels in Barangay Cogorin, this town, on April 23, 2025. The rebel withdrew toward Barangay Santa Rosa and buried assorted firearms and other war materiel belonging to the detached squad of the dismantled Platun Reymark. Recovered from the cache were an improvised explosive device (IED), an improvised hand grenade, a .45-caliber pistol, a .38-caliber pistol, a magazine, and live ammunition, two copies of “Piling Mga Sulating Militar ni Mao Zedong,” and medical supplies. Army Maj. General Arsenio Sadural, commander of the 2nd Infantry Division, said the recovery reflects the continuing effort to consolidate government gains against the remaining communist armed groups in Southern Tagalog. “The dismantling of an armed group does not end with the neutralization of its manpower. We must also account for the weapons, explosives, logistics, and other resources it leaves behind to ensure they can no longer be retrieved and used to rebuild its capabilities,” Sadural said. He also encouraged remaining NPA members to consider the experience of former rebels who are now helping communities move away from armed conflict. “Those who have chosen to return to the folds of the law are showing that there is a meaningful role for them in building peace. We continue to call on those who remain in the armed movement to come home and take the same opportunity to begin again,” Sadural added. The 2nd Division continues to work closely with its partners in the security sector, local government units, former rebels, and communities to locate remaining war materiel and prevent the remnants of dismantled NPA units from rebuilding their capabilities in Southern Tagalog.

Prolonged flooding puts Calasiao, Dagupan residents on edge. CALASIAO, PANGASINAN — Prolonged flooding brought out by the raging rains from the southwest monsoon, or "habagat", has disrupted daily life in parts of Calasiao and Dagupan City, with some residents reportedly dealing with floodwaters for nearly a month. In Calasiao, residents have resorted to riding "kuliglig", a farm machinery, locally used form of transportation, to get through flooded roads and reach their destinations. Floodwaters in some communities have reportedly reached waist level, forcing residents to find alternative ways to move around and, in some cases, seek safer ground. The persistent flooding has also resulted in prolonged class suspensions in affected areas, disrupting the education of students for weeks. In Dagupan City, the flooding is at times aggravated by high tide, which can slow the drainage of floodwaters in low-lying communities. The prolonged inundation has also prompted residents to raise questions about the effectiveness of existing flood-control measures, including road-widening and road-elevation projects, in addressing recurring flooding. Residents say the current situation is among the most prolonged flooding episodes they have experienced in recent memory. While claims that the flooding is the worst or longest since 1972 .: for many residents, the water has stayed far too long.

DPWH, DepEd hold bulk of unused cash use despite improving gov’t spending efficiency in July. Government departments and special purpose funds (SPFs) slightly improved their spending efficiency by end-July 2026, but unused cash authority remained concentrated in public works and education. The latest Department of Budget and Management (DBM) data showed that the overall utilization rate for notices of cash allocation (NCAs) stood at 94.6 percent as of end-July 2026, a 0.6-percentage-point (ppt) increase from the 94 percent recorded in July 2025. Total NCA releases rose to ₱3.13 trillion, roughly 4.7 percent higher than the ₱2.99 trillion recorded a year ago. Of the total, ₱2.96 trillion was utilized, leaving ₱169.9 billion in unused cash authority as of end-July, down from ₱178.2 billion a year ago. Under the government’s accounting framework, these notices act as the primary disbursement authority, allowing agencies to pay for contracted works and services. High utilization typically suggests more efficient procurement and administrative implementation of national programs. Despite the overall national improvement, several major departments saw significant declines in their cash utilization rates. Cash utilization by the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) dropped from 94 percent in July 2025 to 86.2 percent in July 2026, leaving ₱44.2 billion in unused cash—the largest among departments. This came alongside a massive cut in its total NCA releases, which fell from ₱610 billion to ₱320.1 billion. Similarly, the Department of Education (DepEd) saw its utilization rate dip from 97 percent to 93.1 percent, leaving ₱35.3 billion unused—more than triple the ₱10.7 billion recorded a year ago. The Department of Transportation’s (DOTr) cash utilization also fell from 92 percent to 85.7 percent, leaving ₱7 billion unused. Other agencies reporting declines were the Presidential Communications Office (PCO), which dropped from 86 percent to 72 percent; the Office of the President (OP), from 89 percent to 69.4 percent; and the Civil Service Commission (CSC), from 92 percent to 73.3 percent. Further, the Department of Finance’s (DOF) utilization rate fell from 96 percent to 90 percent, leaving ₱1.5 billion unused. This decline came alongside a massive reduction in total releases to the department, which plummeted from ₱50.8 billion to ₱15 billion. In contrast, several departments and agencies showed notable resilience and improved efficiency. For one, the Department of National Defense (DND) saw a solid improvement, with its utilization rate rising to 98.4 percent from 93 percent a year ago. Other agencies that posted improved utilization rates included the Department of Agriculture (DA), which rose to 79.4 percent from 72 percent; the Office of the Ombudsman, which increased to 96.5 percent from 93 percent; and the Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD), which inched up to 91.4 percent from 91 percent. Under SPFs, allocations to local government units (ALGU) achieved a 100-percent utilization rate, up from 99 percent. However, some agencies that previously reported solid performance lost ground. The Judiciary saw its utilization rate drop to 91.8 percent, while the Commission on Elections (Comelec) fell to 76.9 percent.

DA moves to stop solar projects from encroaching on farmland. The Department of Agriculture (DA) is proposing a geofencing program to protect agricultural land from rapidly expanding solar power projects in a bid to strengthen the country’s food security. Agriculture Secretary Francisco Tiu Laurel Jr. said his agency is pushing to geofence around three million hectares of flat agricultural land, particularly rice-producing areas, to prevent them from being converted into solar farms. Geofencing creates digital geographic boundaries around priority agricultural areas, offering renewable energy (RE) developers a clear guide on where projects should not be located. “We need energy security, but it cannot come at the cost of food security. The country must be able to keep the lights on without putting at risk the land that keeps food on Filipino tables,” Tiu Laurel said in a statement on Monday, Aug. 31. He noted that the plan aims to identify up to 2,000 flat rice lands for geofencing, ensuring they remain dedicated to agricultural production. The DA added that this list of priority lands will be cross-checked against existing and awarded energy projects to prevent overlaps. Tiu Laurel said the initiative was proposed during a recent meeting with Department of Energy (DOE) Secretary Sharon Garin to address the balance between the country’s solar capacity expansion and food production. Additionally, the DA is lobbying for a program that would allow farmers and fisherfolk to directly benefit from the ongoing RE transition through lower electricity costs. Under this proposal, RE suppliers under the Green Energy Auction, Green Energy Option, and the Retail Competition and Open Access framework could connect directly with qualified agricultural end-users. Potential beneficiaries include farms, fishponds, irrigation systems, post-harvest facilities, rice mills, cold storage plants, slaughterhouses, and other food production operations. The DOE is currently examining how RE suppliers and distribution utilities can participate in the proposed initiative. In the meantime, the DA and DOE are working to develop a farm-to-energy framework alongside the Energy Regulatory Commission (ERC) to explore further ways organized agricultural groups can benefit from RE. “The framework will help proponents under the agricultural energy category lower electricity costs, generate savings, and strengthen incomes across the sector,” said Agriculture Undersecretary Roger Navarro. The DA announced it will sign a memorandum of agreement with the DOE in October to formalize the partnership and expedite the development of the recommended programs. “Our goal now, for both the DOE and the DA, is to ensure that both of these pressing needs of Filipinos are addressed in a way that benefits the country without sacrificing one for the other,” Tiu Laurel said.

Honorary degree given to Marcos for his contributions, Palace says. Malacañang has defended President Marcos for receiving honoris causa amid criticisms, saying it was given to him in recognition of his contrubutions as the higest-ranking official in the country. Last week, Marcos received honoris causa, the highest honorary degree of the Pamantasan ng Lungsod ng Maynila, when he graced the university's 58th commencement exercises. The feat has since drawn criticism. Palace Press Officer and Communications Undersecretary Claire Castro clarified that the honorary degree is not earned through traditional academic studies, attending law school, or passing the bar examinations. "Ang titulong honoris causa ay isang honorary degree. Ito ay isang pagkilala o parangal para sa taong mataas ang naabot na posisyon. May mga mahalagang naiambag sa komunidad o mga nagawa para sa bansa (The title honoris causa is an honorary degree. It is a form of recognition or distinction given to a person who has attained a high position, made significant contributions to the community, or accomplished something of importance for the country)," Castro said on Monday, Aug. 31. "At hindi ito nakukuha sa pamamagitan ng tradisyonal na pag-aaral, pagpasok sa law school, o pagpasa sa bar examinations (It is not earned through traditional academic studies, attending law school, or passing the bar examinations)," Castro explained. The Palace official stressed that perhaps many "do not fully understand the term honoris causa." She also alleged that some of those criticizing the President for receiving the honorary degree are "obstructionists at destabilizers." "Ang mga tumutuligsa rito ay mga taong kung hindi man mapagmataas ay mga kumakalaban sa Pangulo, the usual obstructionists at destabilizers, o yung mga sumasakay lang sa nakikita sa social media, pero hindi nauunawaan ang totoong issue (Those criticizing it are people who, if not being arrogant, are either opposed to the President, the usual obstructionists and destabilizers, or simply jumping on the bandwagon based on what they see on social media without understanding the real issue)," Castro said. With this, the Palace spokesperson underscored the need to clarify it to prevent people from being misled. "Mahalagang malinawan ibang kababayan natin na naloloko ng iba gamit ang fake news o ng pagiging mapagmataas lamang (It is important to clarify this for our fellow Filipinos who may be misled by others through fake news or simply because of arrogance)," Castro said. Castro cited several actions Marcos has taken during his presidency that make him worthy of the recognition. "Huwag natin kalimutan ang pagtindig pa lamang ng ating Pangulong, Pangulong Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. sa karapatan natin sa West Philippine Sea (Let us not forget how our President, Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr., has stood up for our rights in the West Philippine Sea)," Castro said. "Ang pagpaputol ng 300-meter floating barrier na inilagay ng China Coast Guard sa Scarborough Shoal noong September 2023 para harangin ang ating mangingisda na makapasok at makapangisda sa traditional fishing lagoon ay isang gawain ng isang matapat na leader (The removal of the 300-meter floating barrier installed by the China Coast Guard at Scarborough Shoal in September 2023 to prevent our fishermen from entering and fishing in their traditional fishing lagoon was an act of a steadfast leader)," Castro added. She also cited Marcos' move to initiate investigations into corruption allegations and his response to the fuel crisis caused by the conflict in the Middle East. Castro further mentioned the actions taken for distressed and displaced overseas Filipino workers in Qatar and Russia.

Joshua Garcia, Julia Barretto surprise fans with ‘It’s Showtime’ reunion. Joshua Garcia and Julia Barretto surprised fans when they appeared together on ABS-CBN’s noontime program “It’s Showtime” on Monday, giving their followers another dose of JoshLia chemistry. So reuniting with him on the set is always something I look forward [to] ,” she said. Filipinos spent so much on streaming, apps that taxes hit ₱17 billion—BIR. Tax collections from foreign digital service providers reached ₱17.5 billion in the first six months of the year, driven by higher consumer adoption and improved compliance among global technology platforms. Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR) Commissioner Charlito Martin R. Mendoza told the Manila Bulletin that revenues collected by the government’s main tax agency from non-resident digital service providers (DSPs) have seen “encouraging” growth on the back of robust compliance. Collections from foreign DSPs surged more than threefold during the first semester compared to the ₱6.6 billion logged in the initial six months of the value-added tax (VAT) on digital services program. The government began collecting the 12-percent consumption levy on DSPs in June 2025, covering both business-to-business (B2B) and business-to-consumer (B2C) transactions. It bears noting that the first-half collection already accounts for three-fourths of the national government’s full-year target of ₱23.1 billion. Mendoza said the overwhelming expansion in collections from this segment is an “encouraging sign that implementation is gaining traction.” Between B2B and B2C, Mendoza noted that the latter emerged as the “slightly bigger” contributor, though B2B transactions still made a substantial showing. “This means the growth is broad-based and reflects increasing digital activity from both individual consumers and businesses,” Mendoza said. Major global platforms registered with the BIR include Meta, Google Asia, Netflix, Disney, Canva, Spotify, LinkedIn, Microsoft, OpenAI, and Valve. While substantial, Mendoza noted that the expansion in tax haul was an anticipated development “as compliance improves and more digital transactions are properly captured.” For the BIR, this trend implies that the digital VAT law is proving effective. “It is helping level the playing field between local and foreign digital service providers, improving tax compliance, and ensuring that the growing digital economy contributes its fair share to government revenues and, ultimately, to public services for our people,” Mendoza said. However, the BIR chief believes it is still “too early” to make a definitive projection for the full year, responding to a query on whether the medium-term program necessitates upward revisions due to the robust first-half haul. Mendoza also demurred on betting whether the first-semester figure would double by year-end to reach roughly ₱35 billion. He explained that fourth-quarter collections are due in January 2027, deferring the complete tally of the current fiscal year's returns. Of the government's tax reform measures, only the VAT on digital services brought in additional revenues. Meanwhile, the Capital Markets Efficiency Promotion Act (CMEPA) and the CREATE MORE Act reduced revenues by ₱2.3 billion and ₱342 million, respectively. Revenue losses from CMEPA are expected to more than double to ₱4.9 billion in 2026, before dropping by 5.5 percent to ₱4.6 billion in 2027. Incurred losses from lowering corporate income taxes (CIT) under the CREATE MORE Act are projected to nearly triple to ₱981 million this year and swell further by 68.2 percent to ₱1.7 billion next year. VAT collections from digital services form part of the BIR's overall tax collection, which stood at ₱1.63 trillion, boosted by higher returns from corporate income tax, personal income tax, VAT, other percentage taxes, and miscellaneous taxes. More recently, the BIR collected ₱1.99 trillion—up 5.3 percent from a year earlier—as improved taxpayer services helped strengthen compliance and boost receipts.
